title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Multi-cycle iterative divider: take DIV/REM off the single-cycle EX path
motivation:
Fmax is 5.442 MHz because the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) runs
forward_unit -> ex_stage operand mux -> alu -> EX/MEM register, and the
alu contains four fully combinational 32-bit dividers (signed/unsigned
`/` and `%`). CoreMark executes essentially no DIV/REM inside the timed
region, so the single-cycle divider buys no iterations/cycle while
costing ~9x in Fmax and ~10K of the 12.3K LUT4.

Measured during hypothesis generation (Gowin, place option 0, scratch
copy of the RTL, same bench wrapper):
  - baseline:                         5.44 MHz, 12312 LUT, 6 DSP
  - DIV/REM arms stubbed to 0:       49.08 MHz,  2071 LUT, 6 DSP
  - MUL and DIV/REM arms stubbed:    43.76 MHz,  2016 LUT, 0 DSP
So the divider alone is the bottleneck. The multiplier (already in DSP
blocks) is NOT limiting: removing it changes nothing beyond placement
noise, so it must stay single-cycle (making MUL multi-cycle would only
lose IPC). With the divider gone the worst paths are ~25.6 ns:
(a) ID/EX -> forward mux -> branch compare -> redirect -> IF NOP mux ->
hazard/regfile read -> ID/EX, and (b) ID/EX -> forward mux -> alu ->
EX/MEM.alu_result D-input, which Gowin merges into the dmem BSRAM
address register. Projected fitness ~2.226e-6 iter/cycle x ~45-49 MHz
= ~100-109 iter/s versus 12.12.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational dividers with ONE shared sequential radix-2
restoring divider (1 quotient bit per cycle, ~35 cycles per
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU) beside the ALU in EX, stalling IF/ID/EX while it
runs. Its internal path is one 33-bit subtract + 2:1 mux between
registers, and its operands are latched from the post-forward rs1/rs2,
so the forward-mux -> divide chain leaves the timed netlist. MUL* stay
exactly as they are. Expected Fmax ~45-49 MHz at <1% IPC loss, i.e.
roughly 8-9x fitness (the +50 below is only the schema cap).

Mechanics the implementation must get right:
1. rtl/div_unit.sv: start/busy/done handshake. The start cycle latches
   the RAW operands and op flags only (no negate/compare on the
   forwarded operands, that path is already co-critical). Then: one
   PREP cycle (absolute values, from registers), 32 shift-subtract
   cycles, one FIX cycle (sign correction + RV32M corner cases:
   x/0 -> quotient all-ones, remainder = dividend; INT_MIN/-1 ->
   quotient INT_MIN, remainder 0), then `done` with a registered
   result. `done` and the result are STICKY until the DIV actually
   leaves EX (EX/MEM captures it), so a dmem_stall on the done cycle
   is harmless.
2. ex_stage: is_div = in.valid && alu_op in {DIV,DIVU,REM,REMU};
   ex_busy = is_div && !done. ex_busy must depend only on registers
   (ID/EX alu_op, divider state), never on operand values. Start on the
   first cycle the DIV sits in EX (forwarded operands are valid then,
   also under dmem_stall because MEM/WB keeps its data). Also latch the
   post-forward rs1/rs2 into hold registers and use those for
   EX/MEM.rs1_val / rs2_val / write_data when the DIV finally moves on:
   the EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding sources drain away during the
   divide, so re-evaluating the forward muxes on the done cycle would
   give stale ID/EX values (wrong rvfi_rs*_rdata).
3. Pipeline control while ex_busy: PC holds (stall_if), ID/EX HOLDS
   (stall_id = 1, flush_id = 0; a DIV never raises redirect or
   load_use for itself), EX/MEM captures a bubble ('0) so MEM and WB
   drain and retire normally. dmem_stall keeps priority: when it is
   active EX/MEM holds exactly as today.
4. The divider result must enter the datapath as a registered input to
   the EXISTING alu result mux (in place of the `/` `%` arms), not as an
   extra mux level after it: alu -> EX/MEM.alu_result -> dmem BSRAM
   address is one of the two ~25.6 ns paths that will set the new Fmax.
5. ALTOPS consistency: under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS keep the same
   start/busy/done handshake and stall path but finish in 1-2 cycles,
   returning (a - b) ^ <existing per-op constant> from the latched
   operands. A 35-cycle divide cannot retire inside the depth-20 BMC
   (insn / liveness / cover checks), while a short ALTOPS divide still
   has riscv-formal exercise the hold, bubble and operand-capture
   logic. MUL ALTOPS arms are untouched.

RVFI contract unchanged: single retirement on channel 0, order +1 per
valid MEM/WB, pc_wdata = pc + 4 for DIV/REM, bubbles have valid = 0.

title: Multi-cycle M-unit: iterative divider + registered multiplier out of the single-cycle EX path
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.442 MHz because the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells,
~150 logic levels) runs MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> EX operand mux ->
alu.sv combinational 32-bit divider (`/` and `%`, signed + unsigned) ->
EX/MEM alu_result -> dmem address. The three combinational 64-bit
multipliers (mul_ss / mul_uu / mul_su, 6 DSP) sit behind it as the next
wall. Every instruction pays a ~200 ns clock for an operation CoreMark
does not execute in its kernels: compiling the four CoreMark kernel files
with the bench flags (-O3 -march=rv32im) gives 0 static div/rem
instructions and only 15 static mul sites (13 in core_matrix, 2 in
core_list_join), so DIV/REM latency is irrelevant to the score and MUL
is a few percent of the dynamic mix. IPC is already ~2.2 CoreMark/MHz, so the whole fitness gap
is cycle time: removing the divider and multiplier from the single-cycle
EX cone should move Fmax from ~5 MHz to the ordinary 5-stage range
(tens of MHz), an order-of-magnitude fitness gain for a 1-3% IPC cost.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure EX so that M-extension ops are executed by a separate
multi-cycle unit (new rtl/muldiv.sv) with a busy/done handshake that
stalls the front of the pipeline, while all RV32I ops stay single-cycle
in alu.sv.

1. Divider: radix-2 restoring (shift-subtract) iterative divider, one
   quotient bit per cycle, ~34 cycles (setup with |a|,|b| and sign
   capture, 32 iterations, sign fix-up). One 33-bit subtract + mux per
   cycle. DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU share it. RV32M corner cases come out of the
   datapath or a registered special-case select: div-by-0 -> quotient
   all-ones, remainder = dividend; INT_MIN/-1 -> quotient INT_MIN,
   remainder 0.
2. Multiplier: ONE 33x33 signed multiplier replaces the three 64-bit
   ones (a_ext = {a_signed & a[31], a}, b_ext = {b_signed & b[31], b};
   MUL/MULHU: unsigned,unsigned; MULH: signed,signed; MULHSU:
   signed,unsigned). Operands are registered (post-forward) at the end
   of the first EX cycle, the product is registered at the end of the
   second, and the low/high half is selected into EX/MEM in the third:
   reg -> DSP -> reg, so Gowin can pack the input/output registers into
   the DSP block. MUL = 2 stall cycles; no multiplier logic in the
   forward-mux -> ALU -> EX/MEM cone.
3. Handshake: decoder emits a registered ctrl bit `is_muldiv` (plus
   is_div to pick the sub-unit). `ex_busy = id_ex.valid && is_muldiv &&
   !md_done` is built from flops only. While ex_busy: stall_if and
   stall_id hold PC and ID/EX (no flush), EX/MEM captures a bubble
   (valid=0, reg_write=0, mem_read/mem_write=0) unless dmem_stall is
   holding it, and MEM/WB drains normally. When done, the result is held
   in the unit until EX/MEM actually accepts it (!stall_ex_mem), then
   done clears. dmem_stall keeps its existing precedence (hold
   everything back to MEM); the unit may keep iterating underneath it.
4. Operand capture: the unit latches the POST-FORWARD rs1/rs2 in the
   first cycle the M-op is in EX. This is mandatory, not an
   optimisation: while the M-op waits, the producers in EX/MEM and
   MEM/WB drain into the regfile and the forwarding sources disappear,
   while ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val are stale. The EX/MEM rs1_val/rs2_val
   (RVFI rs*_rdata) for M-ops must come from the latched copies too.
   The first-cycle forward is always valid: an instruction in ID/EX is
   never wrong-path (branches resolve in EX), a LOAD in EX/MEM can never
   be the EX/MEM forward source (load-use stall), and MEM/WB data fields
   are retained under hold_mem_wb.
5. Redirect is unaffected (M-ops never redirect). The load-use hazard
   and flush_id logic are unchanged except that ex_busy joins the
   stall_if/stall_id terms and must not turn a hold into a bubble.
6. RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS: the same FSM/handshake is kept under formal (so
   riscv-formal proves the new stall, operand-capture and bubble logic),
   but the result is the ALTOPS XOR formula of the latched operands and
   the divider's iteration count is shortened under the ifdef so the M-op
   retires well inside the BMC depth and the liveness bound. The real
   (non-ALTOPS) branch must stay bit-exact RV32M (test_alu vectors +
   cosim CRCs).

Measured proxy (Gowin P&R, placement option 0, this RTL with the mul/div
arms simply deleted from alu.sv, i.e. the EX cone the new design has):
Fmax 46.7 MHz, 21 logic levels, 1922 LUT, 0 DSP, vs 5.44 MHz / 150
levels / 12312 LUT today. The remaining worst path there is regfile ->
EX forward/branch compare -> redirect -> if_stage NOP mux -> decoder ->
ID/EX (26.7 ns), which has nothing to do with the M unit, so the M unit
must only stay off that path (register-to-register, <20 levels) to
realise ~8.5x Fmax. Formal note: wrapper_si ties both ready inputs to 1
and BMC depth is 20, so ALTOPS latency must be a few cycles at most.

Expected result: the 200 ns divider path and the DSP multiplier path are
gone; the new worst path should be forward-mux -> 32-bit adder/shifter
-> ALU result mux -> EX/MEM / dmem-address BSRAM, or forward-mux ->
branch compare -> redirect -> PC, i.e. roughly 12-20 ns (50-80 MHz) on
the GW2AR-18. CoreMark cycles rise only by 2 per MUL and ~34 per DIV/REM
(a low single-digit percent), so fitness should rise by roughly 8-12x
(far beyond the +50 cap of the expected_impact field). LUT count should
also fall sharply (12.3k -> a few thousand) because the array divider
disappears, which further helps routing delay.

changes.description: New module. Inputs: clock, reset, start (first EX cycle of a valid M-op), op (ALU_MUL..ALU_REMU), post-forward a/b, accept (EX/MEM takes the result). Outputs: done, result[31:0], latched a/b for RVFI. Contains (a) the reg->33x33 signed multiply->reg multiplier with low/high select, (b) the radix-2 restoring divider FSM (IDLE / ITER with 5-bit counter / FIX) with registered sign and special-case handling for div-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1, (c) a done flag that stays set until accept. Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the result is the ALTOPS formula on the latched operands and the latency is a short fixed count; the real branch is bit-exact RV32M.

Remove the combinational `*`, `/`, `%` arms (and their ALTOPS stand-ins) so alu.sv is a pure single-cycle RV32I ALU (add/sub/logic/slt/shift/lui); M-op codes fall to the default arm. M-extension results now come from muldiv.sv.

Instantiate muldiv; generate start (valid M-op in ID/EX, unit idle, not done) and accept (!stall); export ex_busy. Select muldiv result into reg_q.alu_result for M-ops; use the unit's latched operands for reg_q.rs1_val/rs2_val on M-ops. While ex_busy and not dmem-stalled, load a bubble into EX/MEM (valid=0, ctrl cleared) instead of the instruction; keep the existing hold on dmem stall.

Add ex_busy input. stall_if and stall_id include ex_busy (hold PC and ID/EX); flush_id must not fire because of load_use/redirect terms while ex_busy holds ID/EX (an M-op in EX never redirects; the load-use bubble is re-evaluated once the M-op leaves). imem stall handling (flush_if) stays as is so a fetched instruction is not lost while ID is held.
Add is_muldiv (and is_div) bits to ctrl_t so EX gets a registered one-bit M-op qualifier instead of decoding alu_op in the stall path.
Drive the new is_muldiv / is_div ctrl bits inside the already validated funct7=0000001 R-type arm (default 0; is_illegal handling unchanged).
Wire the new decoder outputs into ctrl_decoded; verify the IF->ID hand-off does not drop a delivered instruction when stall_id is asserted by ex_busy for many consecutive cycles.
Route ex_busy from ex_stage to hazard_unit; no top-level IO change (nret stays 1).
Retarget the M-extension vectors (30+ per op, incl. div-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1) at the multi-cycle muldiv unit via start/done; keep the RV32I vectors on the combinational alu.

Add pipeline tests for M-ops whose operands are forwarded from EX/MEM and MEM/WB (operand-capture hazard), back-to-back MUL/DIV, M-op result consumed by the next instruction / branch / store, and M-ops under imem and dmem stalls.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-002-r1s1 (regression, +753.22%): "Regression" here means it lost to the divider-only sibling that landed in the same round (103.41 vs 106.74), not to the 12.12 baseline: additionally moving MUL into the multi-cycle unit (one registered 33x33 reg -> DSP -> reg multiplier, 2 stall cycles per MUL) bought no Fmax — div-only 47.9 MHz, full M-unit 48.4 MHz and the no-M-logic-at-all proxy 46.7 MHz all sit inside the seed spread on the same ~26 ns forward-mux -> branch-compare -> redirect -> IF/decoder -> ID/EX wall — while the MUL stalls cost ~4% CoreMark cycles (~4.49M -> ~4.68M implied by fitness/Fmax, i.e. ~9K dynamic MULs per iteration out of core_matrix inner loops, well above the 1-3% guessed from "15 static mul sites"), so only make a block multi-cycle when it is the measured binding path, size the IPC cost from dynamic op counts rather than static sites, and treat each stall cycle added to MUL as ~2% fitness that a future multiplier re-pipelining must more than win back in Fmax.

title: BTB-less fetch-stage branch predictor: predecode + gshare direction + JAL always-taken, verified in EX
motivation:
The core has no branch prediction: every taken branch, JAL and JALR is
resolved in EX and costs one bubble (flush of the instruction sitting in
IF/ID). CoreMark is ~20% conditional branches (well over half taken) plus
~3% jumps, so roughly 0.14-0.16 bubble cycles per instruction out of a
measured CPI of ~1.5-1.6 (fitness 12.12 = 2.227 CoreMark/MHz x 5.442 MHz)
are pure taken-control-flow penalty.
Two properties of this pipeline make a predictor unusually cheap here:
(1) imem is read combinationally and IF/ID is a combinational bundle, so
the fetched instruction word is visible in the same cycle its PC is live.
The exact target of a branch/JAL (pc + imm) can be computed in the fetch
cycle itself - no BTB, no target aliasing, zero-bubble correct predictions.
(2) Redirects are only raised from EX, in the very cycle the wrong-path
instruction is in IF. So any instruction that is accepted into ID/EX is on
the committed path. Predictor state therefore never needs speculative
repair, and a wrong-path word can never steer the fetch address (redirect
has priority in next_pc), which keeps fetches in bounds (invariant 6).
Timing: Fmax is set by the 200 ns combinational divider path in EX
(fwd -> alu -> EX/MEM). The new fetch path is imemData (a register in the
timed netlist) -> 7-bit opcode predecode -> 32-bit adder -> next-PC mux,
a few ns, so the IPC gain should carry straight through to fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a fetch-stage predictor so correctly predicted taken branches and all
JALs cost zero bubbles; mispredictions still cost exactly one bubble (same
as today's taken-branch cost), so the change can only remove bubbles.

IF stage (combinational on imem_data, same cycle as the PC):
  - predecode: pd_jal = opcode==1101111, pd_br = opcode==1100011.
  - pd_target = pc + (pd_jal ? imm_J : imm_B)  (one 32-bit adder).
  - direction: gshare PHT, 1024 x 2-bit saturating counters, async read,
    index = pc[11:2] ^ ghr[9:0]. No reset on the array (use an `initial`
    zero-fill so it infers LUT-RAM and sims deterministically).
  - pred_taken = imem valid && (pd_jal || (pd_br && pht[idx][1])).
  - next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes — BTB-less fetch-stage branch predictor (gshare + JAL always-taken)

## Result of local checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `verilator --lint-only -Wall` | clean, no warnings |
| `bash formal/run_all.sh` (nret=1 wrapper, ALTOPS) | **53 passed, 0 failed**, first attempt (no fix attempts used) |
| cosim (`tools.eval.cosim`, selftest + CoreMark, with/without stalls) | **passed**, 2 ELFs |
| cocotb unit tests (`make test TARGET=bench`) | 6 passed (incl. new `test_branch_predictor.py`, 7 cases) |
| CoreMark 2K, `--bench --istall --dstall` | **4,188,121** bracketed cycles (baseline 4,491,485) → **+7.24 % iterations/cycle**; CRCs correct, `oob=false` |
| Gowin timing, all 3 placement options | 5.168 / 5.478 / 5.478 MHz → median **5.478 MHz** (baseline 5.14 / 5.442 / 5.442, median 5.442) |

Expected fitness from these numbers: 5.478 MHz × 2.3877 iter/Mcycle ≈ **13.08** vs
baseline 12.12 (≈ +7.9 %). The cycle count is within 20 cycles of the
hypothesis' prototype figure (4,188,141).

Critical path is unchanged: `u_mem/reg_q.rd → u_fwd → u_ex → u_alu (divider) → dmem
address`, 198.8 ns. The predictor does not appear in the worst paths.
Area: logic 12312 → 12987, registers 460 → 483, LUT-RAM 8 → 72 (the PHT
inferred as distributed RAM, as intended), BSRAM/DSP unchanged.

## What changed

- `rtl/branch_predictor.sv` (new): 1024 × 2-bit gshare PHT, async read, sync
  write, `initial` zero-fill, no reset on the array; 10-bit GHR (reset to 0).
  Lookup: `idx = pc[11:2] ^ ghr`, returns the 2-bit counter. Update: writes the
  saturated counter and shifts the GHR on the same enable.
- `rtl/core_pkg.sv`: `if_id_t` and `id_ex_t` gain `pred_taken`, `pht_idx[9:0]`,
  `pht_ctr[1:0]`.
- `rtl/if_stage.sv`: predecode of `imem_data` for JAL / BRANCH, one 32-bit
  adder for `pd_target = pc + imm_J/imm_B`,
  `next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : pred_taken ? pd_target : pc+4`.
  Prediction fields are zeroed in the IF/ID bundle when flush/redirect turns
  the output into a NOP.
- `rtl/id_stage.sv`: latches the three prediction fields into ID/EX (cleared by
  reset/flush with the rest of the register).
- `rtl/ex_stage.sv`: `redirect = in.valid && (actual_taken != in.pred_taken)`
  with `actual_taken = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault`. Exports
  `bp_upd_en/idx/ctr/taken` for training. `pc_next` / RVFI / trap logic
  untouched.
- `rtl/core.sv`: instantiates `branch_predictor`; update enable is
  `bp_upd_en && !stall_ex_mem && !reset` so a branch held in EX across a dmem
  stall trains exactly once.
- `rtl/hazard_unit.sv`: unchanged (`redirect` now means "mispredict").
- `test/test_branch_predictor.py` (new): untrained entry predicts not-taken,
  taken / not-taken saturation, prediction bit flips at counter = 2, GHR shift
  and index XOR, no update without enable, entry independence.
- `test/test_pipeline.py`: added `branch_predictor.sv` to the hard-coded
  source list (otherwise the core no longer elaborates in that test).

## Deviations from the hypothesis plan

1. **Counter is carried with the instruction instead of re-read at update.**
   The plan's update port was (idx, direction, enable), which implies a second
   async read of `pht[upd_idx]` in EX. I carry the 2-bit counter read at fetch
   down to EX (`pht_ctr`, +2 flops in ID/EX) and write `saturate(pht_ctr,
   taken)`. The array then has exactly one async read port and one sync write
   port, which is the plain simple-dual-port LUT-RAM pattern (Gowin inferred
   64 extra LUT-RAM cells, no flop fallback). The only behavioural difference
   is when two consecutive branches hit the same PHT entry (the younger one
   trains from a counter that is one update stale); the measured cycle count
   differs from the prototype by 20 cycles out of 4.19 M.
2. **Misaligned targets are not predicted.** `pred_taken` is additionally
   gated by `!pd_imm[1]`. Such a JAL/branch traps in EX and falls through, so
   predicting it could only cost a bubble, and it would put a non-word-aligned
   address on `io_imemAddr` for one cycle. With the gate the PC stays 4-byte
   aligned exactly as in the baseline. EX still handles pred=1/actual=0
   generically (needed for illegal branch encodings funct3 = 2/3, which the
   opcode-only predecode can predict taken).
3. **`redirect_target` mux is selected by `in.pred_taken`**, not by
   `actual_taken`: `pred_taken ? pc+4 : is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target`.
   Equivalent whenever `redirect` is asserted (redirect ⇒ actual ≠ pred) and
   keeps the late branch-compare result off the target mux select.
4. **"imem valid" is not a separate term in `pred_taken`.** The PC only takes
   `next_pc` when `!stall` (which includes the imem stall), and the copy of
   `pred_taken` sent to ID is gated by `flush || redirect`, so an explicit
   `imem_ready` input to the fetch stage was unnecessary.
5. Training direction is `branch_taken` (the comparator result) even for a
   taken branch that traps on a misaligned target. Performance-only, and not
   reachable in CoreMark.

## Concerns / things worth knowing

- Predictor state never affects correctness: every prediction is checked in EX
  against the resolved outcome, and the predicted target is `pc + imm` from the
  same instruction word EX uses, so pred=1/actual=1 needs no target compare.
  riscv-formal's `pc_fwd` / `pc_bwd` / `liveness` / `unique` checks all pass
  with the PHT contents unconstrained by reset.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench` as written fails at the `cosim-build` step on this
  core regardless of my change: the Makefile target builds `main.cpp` with the
  default `NRET=2` while `core.yaml` declares `nret: 1`. I ran it as
  `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` (the evaluator's `tools.eval.cosim` sets
  NRET from core.yaml itself), which is the run reported above.
- Fmax on this core is placement-noise dominated (baseline options span
  5.14–5.442 MHz on an identical netlist), so the +0.7 % median Fmax I measured
  should be read as "unchanged", not as a gain. The scored improvement is the
  IPC part.
- JALR (incl. function returns) is still never predicted and costs one bubble,
  as specified. A return-address stack would be the natural follow-up.
lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-003-r1s2 (regression, +7.92%): "Regression" again means it lost to the same-round divider sibling (13.08 vs 106.74) — against its own 12.12 parent the BTB-less fetch predictor was a clean +7.9%, all of it IPC (4,491,485 -> 4,188,121 CoreMark cycles = +7.24% iter/cycle, within 20 cycles of the Verilator prototype; formal 53/53 first try; +675 LUT4, +23 FF, +64 LUT-RAM), so an IPC-only idea built on a base whose Fmax is ~9x off cannot win a round, but this one is orthogonal to div_unit and worth re-porting onto the ~48 MHz champion: because imem is read combinationally and IF/ID is not a flop, opcode predecode of the fetched word (JAL always-taken, BRANCH via 1024x2 gshare, JALR never) plus one `pc + imm_J/imm_B` adder gives exact zero-bubble targets with no BTB, and because redirects only fire from EX while the wrong-path instruction is still in IF, the PHT/GHR train only on committed branches and need no speculative repair (a mispredict is the same single bubble as before, so it can only remove bubbles); keep what passed — carry pht_idx/pht_ctr in ID/EX so the PHT is one async-read + one sync-write LUT-RAM, gate training with !stall_ex_mem so a held branch trains once, `redirect = valid && (actual_taken != pred_taken)` with redirect_target selected by the registered pred_taken, and `!imm[1]` gating so the PC stays word-aligned — but its "no Fmax cost" was only shown under the 199 ns divider path that hides everything: on the champion the verify XOR lands on the binding forward-mux -> branch-compare -> redirect -> IF wall (the fetch side is nearly free in the timed netlist, since fpga/core_bench.sv drives io_imemData from an LFSR register), so it nets positive only if it costs < ~6.7% Fmax (~3 MHz of 47.9).

title: IPC-neutral EX-wall trim: ID-precomputed forward selects, redirect off the fetch NOP mux, LUT-RAM regfile, direct MUL operands, pre-merged WB data
motivation:
The champion (47.946 MHz median, 106.74) is bound by a ~21 ns EX-stage wall
whose length is mostly bookkeeping at the head and tail of the path, not
arithmetic. Measured during hypothesis generation with the scoring flow
(Gowin, same bench wrapper, scratch copies of the RTL, place options 0/1/2),
each step stacked on the previous one, none of them changing a single
pipeline cycle of behaviour:
  champion                                   46.24 / 47.95 / 47.95  MHz
  A redirect removed from IF NOP mux              -  / 52.03 /   -
  A+B forward selects precomputed in ID      52.08 / 52.60 / 52.60
  A+B+C regfile as LUT-RAM (not BSRAM)       58.55 / 61.03 /   -
  A+B+C+D MUL operands straight from rs1/rs2 65.22 / 64.68 / 64.68
  A+B+C+D+E pre-merged MEM/WB wb_data        70.17 / 69.38 / 69.38
Final stack: 2406 LUT, 478 FF, 32 RAM16, 4 BSRAM, 6 DSP; median 69.38 MHz
= +44.7% Fmax. The scratch RTL of the full stack was also run through the
Verilator cosim: selftest + random1/2/3 full-trace compare pass with and
without --istall --dstall, CoreMark CRCs match, and the bracketed CoreMark
cycle count is IDENTICAL to the champion's (4,491,817 cycles), so the whole
Fmax gain converts to fitness (projected ~154).
What each step removes from the path:
A: redirect -> if_stage NOP mux -> hazard load-use compare -> ID/EX CE.
B: two 5-bit rd==rs compares + x0 check + priority encode ahead of the
   forward mux on every EX path.
C: Gowin infers the regfile as BSRAM and absorbs ID/EX.rs?_val into its
   output register, so every operand path starts with BSRAM tC2Q 2.26 ns +
   a bypass LUT (3.7 ns total) instead of a 0.23 ns flop.
D: the is_auipc/alu_src operand muxes (1 LUT + ~1.1 ns route) in front of
   the 3.76 ns DSP multiplier, which is the longest EX leg once A-C are in.
E: the WB mem_to_reg mux in front of the MEM/WB forward leg.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply five small, behaviour-preserving retimings/re-wirings of the EX wall.
Expected: Fmax 47.9 -> ~65-69 MHz, CoreMark cycles unchanged, fitness
~106.7 -> ~145-154.

A. if_stage / hazard_unit: drop `redirect` from the IF/ID payload.
   flush_if = imem_stall only; out.instr = flush ? NOP : imem_data;
   out.valid = !flush. Safe because (1) on redirect && !dmem_stall ID/EX is
   cleared by flush_id anyway, (2) on redirect && dmem_stall ID/EX holds,
   (3) load_use_hazard cannot be raised by the wrong-path word: the
   instruction in EX is a branch/jump, so id_ex_mem_read = 0. redirect
   keeps driving the PC mux and flush_id exactly as today.

B. forward_unit becomes a small clocked block that tracks, one cycle
   ahead, the match bits for the instruction that will be in EX (4 flops:
   m1/m2 per rs; m1 = "EX/MEM.rd matches", m2 = "MEM/WB forwards"):
     ex_mem_w_ok = ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write && !mem_misalign(EX/MEM)
                   (= what MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write will be next cycle)
     a1 = (id_ex.rd  != 0) && (id_ex.rd  == if_id.instr rs field)
     a2 = (ex_mem.rd != 0) && (ex_mem.rd == if_id.instr rs field) && ex_mem_w_ok
     if (reset || flush_id)   m1 <= 0;  m2 <= 0;
     else if (!stall_id)      m1 <= a1; m2 <= a2;               // normal advance
     else if (!dmem_stall)    m1 <= 0;  m2 <= m1 && ex_mem_w_ok; // ex_busy: EX/MEM gets a bubble, MEM/WB takes EX/MEM
     /* else dmem stall: hold (ID/EX, EX/MEM and MEM/WB data all hold) */
   In EX: fwd_sel = (m1 && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write) ? 2'd1 : m2 ? 2'd2 : 2'd0.
   The ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write AND must stay in EX (a register bit, one LUT
   input): a JAL/JALR misalign trap clears reg_write only in EX, too late
   to precompute. dmem_stall here is hazard_unit's stall_ex_mem. This
   reproduces today's forward_unit outputs cycle-for-cycle (same priority,
   same x0 rule, same stall behaviour) - verified by trace cosim.

C. reg_file: store the 32x32 array in distributed LUT-RAM
   ((* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) on the array, synchronous write
   gated by w_en && w_addr != 0, NO per-entry reset loop; add an `initial`
   zero-fill if a simulator/formal gate needs defined power-up contents),
   keep the x0 and write-first bypass read muxes. ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val
   then stay ordinary flops. Fallback if a gate objects to the missing
   reset: syn_ramstyle = "registers" with the reset loop kept (measured
   63.0 MHz at step C, +800 LUT / +1000 FF).

D. alu: feed the three multipliers from the post-forward rs1/rs2 directly
   (two new input ports), not from alu_a/alu_b. MUL* are R-type, so
   alu_a == rs1 and alu_b == rs2 for them; the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arms
   and the div_result leg are unchanged.

E. mem_stage / wb_stage: add a MEM/WB field wb_data <= mem_to_reg ?
   load_data : alu_result (captured in the same non-hold branch as the
   rest of MEM/WB, so it is retained under hold_wb) and make
   wb_stage.w_data = in.wb_data, so the regfile write data / fwd_mem_wb
   leg is a plain register. read_data / alu_result stay for RVFI.

After A-E the worst path is forward-select flop -> 2-LUT forward mux ->
DSP multiply -> ALU result mux -> is_jump/pc+4 mux -> EX/MEM hold mux ->
dmem BSRAM address (~14.4 ns). Further flattening of that tail is optional
and not needed for the projected gain; do not add stall cycles or change
pipeline depth - the point of this hypothesis is zero IPC change.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-001-r2s0 (regression, +45.59%): "Regression" only means it lost the round to sibling hyp-20261124-002-r2s1 by 0.8% (155.40 vs 156.68; 69.8 vs 70.4 MHz, inside the place-option spread) — against the 106.74 parent it was a clean +45.6% at an identical 4,491,817 CoreMark cycles, within 1% of the ~154 projected by stacking the five edits one at a time in scratch synth and cosim-checking the stack before filing (redirect off the IF NOP mux +4.1 MHz, forward selects as 4 ID-precomputed match flops +0.6, regfile pinned to LUT-RAM +8.4 because Gowin otherwise infers BSRAM and absorbs ID/EX.rs?_val into its 2.26 ns-tC2Q output register, MUL fed from rs1/rs2 ahead of the is_auipc/alu_src muxes +3.6, pre-merged MEM/WB wb_data +4.7) — but this EX-resident select-flop design (2417 LUT/478 FF) and the sibling's ID-resident bypass with operand-capture ID/EX (2509 LUT/519 FF) both stop at ~70 MHz, so they are alternatives that do not stack (two slots of one round on the same wall discards one of the wins) and operand-finding bookkeeping is now exhausted: the shared ~14.3 ns wall is operand flop -> DSP 32x32 multiply (3.76 ns), tied within 3 ps with the alu_src mux -> barrel-shifter leg, -> ~6.2 ns of ALU result mux -> is_jump/pc+4 mux -> EX/MEM hold mux -> dmem BSRAM address at ~50% routing, so shortening the MUL leg alone cannot move Fmax and the next Fmax idea must cut that post-arithmetic tail for both legs at once (untested: drive the dmem address from a dedicated rs1+imm adder so MUL/shift results only have to reach a flop); of this stack only the direct-MUL-operand rewiring and the pre-merged wb_data are absent from the new champion, worth porting only if its timing report shows the DSP leg ahead of the shifter or the WB write-mux -> regfile-bypass leg binding.

title: Bypass-at-decode: resolve operand forwarding in ID (operand-capture ID/EX) and take redirect off the decode/hazard path
motivation:
The champion (47.9 MHz, 106.74) is bound by one 26.9 ns / 33-cell loop:
MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit compare -> EX forward mux -> branch compare ->
redirect -> if_stage NOP mux -> hazard_unit load-use compare -> ID/EX
(flush/CE). Its sibling path (forward compare -> forward mux -> ALU ->
dmem BSRAM address) is ~25.6 ns. Both start with the same ~5-6 logic
levels of "find the operand" work (rd/rs compares, priority, 3:1 mux, the
WB write mux) that sit IN SERIES with the ALU and the branch comparator,
and the branch path additionally ends with ~5 levels (NOP mux -> decoder
field -> load-use compare -> flush) that are logically redundant on a
redirect. LESSONS show that making MUL/DIV multi-cycle or adding IPC
features cannot move Fmax while this wall stands. This hypothesis removes
both the head and the tail of the wall WITHOUT changing the cycle-level
behaviour (no new bubbles, no new stalls): CoreMark cycles should stay at
exactly ~4,491,817, so every MHz gained is fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure where forwarding happens: operands are fully resolved at the
ID/EX register INPUT, so the EX stage starts from flops (ID/EX.rs1_val /
rs2_val are always the final architectural values) and contains only
ALU / branch compare / target adders.

1. ID-stage bypass network (replaces forward_unit + the EX forward muxes).
   For rs1 and rs2 (addresses taken from the raw fetched word):
     EX  leg: instruction in ID/EX is valid, reg_write, rd!=0, rd==rs, and
              is not trapping (JAL/JALR misaligned target; only needs
              imm[1] / low 2 bits of rs1+imm) -> data = the value being
              written to EX/MEM.alu_result this cycle
              (is_jump ? pc+4 : alu_result, incl. registered div_result).
     MEM leg: instruction in EX/MEM, reg_write && !mem_misalign, rd!=0,
              rd==rs -> data = mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result.
     WB  leg: the existing write-first regfile bypass (wb_w_en/addr/data).
     else   : regfile read.
   Priority EX > MEM > WB > regfile (youngest writer wins). All selects
   are functions of registers + the fetched word (early); build the mux
   so the late ex_result is the LAST 2:1 stage in front of the ID/EX D
   pin: rs_val_d = sel_ex ? ex_result : early_mux(mem, wb, regfile).
   This is cycle-equivalent to today's forwarding because ID/EX only
   loads on a cycle where the EX instruction also advances
   (stall_id covers dmem_stall and ex_busy), a LOAD in EX still raises
   the existing load-use stall (consumer waits in ID, then takes the MEM
   leg), and a DIV in EX holds ID/EX until div_done, at which point
   alu_result is the final quotient. A value captured into ID/EX is never
   stale, so the hold_rs1/hold_rs2 registers and the "re-forward after a
   stall" hazards disappear; MEM/WB->EX forwarding no longer exists.

2. EX stage: delete fwd_rs1_sel/fwd_rs2_sel muxes, hold_rs1/hold_rs2, and
   use in.rs1_val / in.rs2_val directly for ALU, branch compare, JALR
   target, store data, divider operands and the RVFI rs?_rdata payload.
   Export ex_result and the EX-leg write-enable to ID.

3. Take redirect off the decode path. Today redirect/imem-stall force the
   fetched word to NOP in front of decoder, regfile address and the
   load-use comparator, which is why the critical path continues
   redirect -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id. Instead decode the RAW
   io_imemData unconditionally and apply the kill only as the ID/EX
   synchronous bubble: id_bubble = flush_id || (!stall_id &&
   (redirect || !imem_ready)). The load-use comparator reads raw
   instr[19:15]/[24:20]; a spurious load-use on a killed word is harmless
   because redirect already has priority in the PC register and in
   flush_id, and an imem-stalled word produces a bubble either way.
   redirect then reaches ID/EX through one LUT (sync clear) and the PC
   through its existing mux, instead of through decode + hazard compare.

Expected new worst paths: ID/EX operand flop -> branch compare ->
redirect -> PC / ID/EX clear, and ID/EX operand flop -> ALU -> {EX/MEM +
dmem BSRAM address, 2:1 bypass -> ID/EX D}; roughly 12-14 logic levels
instead of 22, i.e. an estimated 60-68 MHz (vs 47.9) at an unchanged
cycle count -> fitness ~135-150. The single-cycle DSP MUL stays as is; if
(and only if) Gowin timing shows DSP -> bypass -> ID/EX as the new
binding path, drop MUL from the EX leg and treat it like a LOAD for the
load-use stall (result taken from the MEM leg; <=2% cycles), but do not
do this pre-emptively. Check with the Gowin report that reg_file still
maps to RAM (not 1024 flops) now that its read data passes through the
bypass mux before the ID/EX register; if inference degrades, drop the
reset loop in favour of an `initial` zero-fill async-read array.

Verification anchors: CoreMark bracketed cycles must be identical to the
champion (4,491,817) since the change is cycle-equivalent - any
difference is a bug; riscv-formal reg/pc_fwd/unique/liveness cover the

title: Fetch-stage gshare + JAL predictor on the 48 MHz champion, with a depth-neutral EX verify and redirect taken off the IF->hazard->ID/EX path
motivation:
The champion (div_unit, 47.9 MHz, 106.74) still has no branch prediction:
every taken branch / JAL / JALR resolved in EX costs one bubble. The
round-1 BTB-less fetch predictor (hyp-20261124-003-r1s2) measured
4,491,485 -> 4,188,121 CoreMark cycles = +7.24% iter/cycle on this same
pipeline, formal 53/53, +675 LUT4; it lost only because it was built on
the 5.4 MHz parent. It is orthogonal to div_unit (no DIV/REM in the
timed region), so the IPC gain should carry over unchanged.
The open risk named in LESSONS is Fmax: the predictor's verify lands on
the binding redirect path and nets positive only if it costs < ~6.7%
Fmax (and must clear the 4.6% acceptance bar).
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (place option 0: 46.24 MHz,
worst path 26.921 ns arrival, clock launch at 5.33 ns) shows where that
path's time goes: MEM/WB.rd -> forward compare -> rs2 mux -> branch
comparator carry-out is done at 14.75 ns; the remaining 12.2 ns (56% of
the data path) is redirect -> u_if flush/NOP mux (net fanout 102,
18.99 ns) -> NOP-muxed rs1_addr -> u_hazard load-use comparator
(21.6 ns) -> ID/EX hold/clear control (25.9 ns) -> ID/EX and PC flops.
All five reported worst paths have this same tail. That tail is
functionally false: load_use needs a LOAD in EX, redirect needs a
branch/jump in EX, so redirect can never change the load-use result.
So the predictor can be integrated in a way that makes the redirect
path much shorter than today instead of one XOR longer.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-port the proven predictor (opcode predecode of the combinationally
fetched word; JAL always taken, BRANCH via 1024x2-bit gshare LUT-RAM,
JALR never; exact target = pc + imm_J/imm_B from one adder; pred_taken /
pht_idx / pht_ctr carried in ID/EX; `!imm[1]` gating so the PC stays
word aligned; trained only on committed branches, no speculative
repair) onto the champion, with three integration rules that keep the
late comparator output away from everything except the PC mux and a
small ID/EX kill:

1. Redirect off the IF -> decode/hazard path. if_stage no longer muxes
   the instruction to NOP on redirect/flush: the raw imem word always
   feeds decoder, imm_gen, regfile read address and the load-use
   comparator. Wrong-path / stalled fetches are killed only at the
   ID/EX register: hold = dmem_stall | ex_busy (priority, registers
   only), else kill = redirect | imem_stall | load_use, else capture
   (valid=1). Safe because redirect and load_use are mutually exclusive
   (a LOAD in EX never has pred_taken, is_branch or is_jump), and a
   spurious load_use from a garbage word during imem_stall only yields
   the bubble the stall yields anyway (stall_if is already 1). The kill
   clears only valid + ctrl + rd + prediction bits; wide data fields
   (pc, rs*_val, imm, instr) are don't-care in a bubble and get no
   redirect-dependent clear, so the redirect net drives ~30 sync-clears
   plus the 32-bit PC mux instead of 102 loads in front of two more
   comparators.
2. Depth-neutral verify via precomputed polarity. ID registers
   br_sel_lt = funct3[2], br_unsigned = funct3[1],
   br_pol = funct3[0] ^ pred_taken and
   br_chk = is_branch & (pred_taken | !imm[1]) into ID/EX. EX computes
   eq and one signed/unsigned lt, and
     redirect = valid & ((br_chk & ((br_sel_lt ? lt : eq) ^ br_pol))
                         | static_redirect)
   where static_redirect covers jumps exactly as today (JALR and
   unpredicted aligned JAL redirect; predicted JAL does not) and
   "predicted taken but not a legal branch/jump" (illegal funct3 2/3)
   -> redirect to pc+4. Misaligned-target trap semantics are unchanged
   (such instructions are never predicted, trap, and fall through).
   This replaces the 6-way branch_cond case + is_branch AND +
   misalign AND + is_jump OR, so the predictor's XOR is a register
   bit, not a new logic level. redirect_target is selected by
   registered bits only (pred_taken ? pc+4 : is_jump ? jump_target :
   branch_target).
3. Train from EX/MEM, not from EX. pht_idx / pht_ctr / taken are
   captured in the EX/MEM register and the PHT write + GHR shift
   happen the cycle the branch sits in MEM (a branch is never a mem
   op, so it is there exactly one cycle -> trains exactly once). The
   comparator output therefore feeds one flop, never the LUT-RAM write
   data that fans out to ~128 RAM cells.

Expected: the +7.2% IPC measured in round 1 (a mispredict is still one
bubble, so the predictor can only remove bubbles; one-cycle-later
training changes cycle count by noise). Fmax: the redirect path drops
from ~21.6 ns of data delay to roughly comparator + 2 LUTs + PC mux
(~12-13 ns), leaving the forward-mux -> ALU -> EX/MEM / dmem BSRAM
address path (~25.6 ns per LESSONS) as the limit, i.e. Fmax flat to a
few % up rather than down. Fetch-side additions (LFSR-registered
imemData -> predecode -> adder -> next-PC mux, PHT async read) are
short in the timed netlist. Not included on purpose: a return-address
stack / JALR prediction - returns are well under 1% of CoreMark cycles
and verifying a predicted JALR target would add a 32-bit compare behind
the forward mux, on the wall this hypothesis is clearing.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-003-r2s2 (regression, +14.10%): "Regression" only means it lost the round to the bypass-at-decode sibling (121.79 vs 156.68) — against its 106.74 parent the fetch-stage gshare + JAL predictor was a clean +14.1% that split exactly as designed into +7.2% IPC (4,491,817 -> 4,189,486 CoreMark cycles, the same gain as round 1, so one-cycle-later training from EX/MEM costs nothing) and +6.4% Fmax (47.9 -> 51.0 MHz median; on place option 0 46.24 -> 48.64 MHz with all five worst paths now forward-mux -> ALU -> dmem address at 25.85 ns and the redirect path gone from the list), formal 53/53 first try, +630 LUT4 (2381 -> 3011) — so a predictor verify can be made free on the redirect path by registering the compare select / signedness / `funct3[0] ^ pred_taken` polarity and a decode-time static-redirect bit in ID/EX (`redirect = br_chk & ((br_sel_lt ? lt : eq) ^ br_pol) | sr_static`, no `valid &` needed because a bubble clears every enabling bit, only the JALR `(rs1+imm)[1]` alignment check left in EX, `redirect_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : jump_target` on registered selects) and by training the PHT/GHR from the EX/MEM flop so the comparator never drives LUT-RAM write data; but the Fmax half of this win came from killing wrong-path fetches at ID/EX instead of the IF NOP mux, which the new 70.4 MHz champion already contains, so the predictor is still absent from the champion and worth only its ~+7% IPC there (≈168 if Fmax-neutral, break-even at ~4.7 MHz of Fmax loss), unverified on that netlist where the branch compare reads ID-captured operands and the wall is the ~14.3 ns operand flop -> MUL/shifter -> result mux -> dmem address path — re-port it alone rather than racing an Fmax sibling in the same round, since an IPC-only +7% idea has now twice lost its slot to a larger same-round Fmax win despite being correct and orthogonal.

title: Final-operand capture in ID: ALU/MUL start from flops, link and imm selects leave the EX loop
motivation:
The 70.4 MHz champion is bound by the EX loop, not by one endpoint. Gowin
place option 0 of the champion (71.35 MHz) shows: ID/EX.rs2_val flop ->
alu_src mux (0.37 ns + 2.3 ns net, fanout 72) -> DSP multiply (3.78 ns) ->
ALU result mux -> `is_jump ? pc+4` mux -> ex_result -> EX/MEM.alu_result,
the ID bypass mux and the dmem BSRAM address, with the shifter leg tied.
Scratch Gowin runs done while writing this (place option 0, IPC-neutral):
  - dedicated rs1+imm dmem-address register ALONE: 70.98 MHz, no gain. The
    worst path just moves to the same logic ending in EX/MEM.alu_result /
    ID/EX.rs*_val, so LESSONS' "untested address adder" idea is not enough.
  - address register PLUS the EX operand muxes (is_auipc, alu_src) and the
    `is_jump ? pc+4` result mux removed (timing proxy, not functional):
    84.07 MHz (+18%), logic 2406. Gowin then absorbs the operand flops into
    the DSP input registers and the wall becomes ex_result / BSRAM load data
    -> ID bypass mux -> operand register at ~11.6 ns.
Those three muxes are pure select bookkeeping decided by the opcode, so they
can move in front of the ID/EX register at zero cycle cost.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-001-r3s0 (regression, +16.49%): "Regression" only means it lost the round to sibling hyp-20261124-002-r3s1, which built the same idea (182.51 vs 207.43; 82.0 vs 93.2 MHz) — against the 156.68 parent this was a clean +16.5% at an identical 4,491,817 CoreMark cycles (formal 53/53 first try, 2507 LUT/549 FF), so two independent builds now confirm that capturing the final EX operands in ID (pc/imm/link substituted in the early bypass leg, bypass selects gated by opcode-bit use_rs1/use_rs2) together with a dedicated rs1+imm adder into an EX/MEM.mem_addr register breaks the 70 MHz wall, while the address register alone does nothing (70.98 MHz in scratch: the wall just moves to the same cone ending at EX/MEM.alu_result) — but this slot's "no extra timed flops" economy is the likeliest reason it lost: one op_a/op_b pair fed the ALU, the DSP multiplier, the divider, the branch compare and the address adder, Gowin absorbed that pair into the DSP input registers, and the widened operand function (ex_result / MEM leg / regfile / pc-or-imm legs) then sat in front of a 1.76 ns route to the fixed DSP column, leaving BSRAM read data (2.26 ns tC2Q) -> load shift/extend (5 LUTs) -> 3 ID LUTs -> DSP input at 11.94 ns, tied within 0.02 ns with op_a flop -> ALU -> ex_result -> ID mux -> DSP input, whereas the sibling kept plain bypass-only rs1_val/rs2_val flops for MUL/DIV/branch/AGU and added a separate op_a/op_b pair for the ALU alone (+64 FF, 8 vs 9 cells on the load leg, 89.2 MHz as written) and then spent its spare time on the two follow-ups this slot left unbuilt (shifter legs OR-ed last in a flattened ALU result mux -> 90.8, MEM bypass split into an early EX/MEM.alu_result leg and a late load-data leg -> 93.2), so duplicate a register rather than share it when one consumer is a DSP or BSRAM that will absorb it, and nothing from this slot remains to port; also, place options 1 and 2 have returned identical Fmax and paths in every evaluation logged so far, so the scored "median" is simply option 1, and `make timing` (option 0 only) has missed it by -5.9 to +4.4 MHz (here 86.3 vs 82.0 scored, sibling 87.3 vs 93.2; on option 0 the two as-written designs were level at 86.3 vs 85.2, and the real 86.3 beat this hypothesis's own option-0 proxy "ceiling" of 84.07), so size proxies and accept or reject follow-ups with `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`, never option 0 alone.

title: Split the EX result tail: dedicated AGU register for the dmem address + final ALU operands (op_a/op_b) captured in ID, IPC-neutral
motivation:
The 70.4 MHz champion is bound by one ~14.3 ns wall shared by two legs:
ID/EX operand flop -> {DSP 32x32 multiply | alu_src mux -> barrel shifter}
-> 16-way ALU result mux -> is_jump/pc+4 mux -> EX/MEM hold mux -> dmem
BSRAM address pins. fpga/core_bench_si.sv reads dmem asynchronously, so
Gowin absorbs EX/MEM.alu_result[12:2] into the BSRAM address register
(logged worst path: u_id/rs1_val_q_21 -> dmem_1_dmem_1_0_0_s, 10 cells,
~50% routing). Every ALU result has to reach a BSRAM site through the
whole result mux, although only `rs1 + imm` is ever a memory address.
LESSONS (r2s0) left exactly this untested ("drive the dmem address from a
dedicated rs1+imm adder").
Scratch evidence (Gowin, place option 0 ONLY, same flow as `make timing`):
  champion (logged)                               71.347 MHz
  proxy A = this hypothesis                       90.471 MHz (+26.8%), 2641 LUT / 614 FF
  proxy B = A + MUL moved to MEM (late, bubble)   89.415 MHz, 2680 LUT / 647 FF
B is no faster than A, so a late/registered multiplier is NOT part of
this proposal (it would only cost a MUL-use bubble). Limits of the
evidence: one placement option of three (the score is the median), the
proxies were lint-clean but NOT run through cosim or formal, and the
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arms were stripped in the proxy. CoreMark cycles
were not measured; the design adds no stall or bubble, so 4,491,817
cycles is expected by construction, not by test.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the memory address its own endpoint and hand EX its final ALU
inputs, with no change to stalls, bubbles or bypass timing:
(1) AGU. `ID/EX.rs1_val + ID/EX.imm` (flops -> carry chain, no ALU mux)
    feeds a new EX/MEM.mem_addr register under the same stall hold as
    EX/MEM. mem_addr alone drives io_dmemAddr, the byte mask, the
    misalign trap, the load aligner and RVFI mem_addr. alu_result no
    longer reaches the BSRAM.
(2) Operands captured in ID. ID/EX gains op_a/op_b:
      pc_a   = is_auipc | is_jump
      op_a_d = (sel_ex_rs1 && !pc_a) ? ex_result : (pc_a ? pc : rs1_early)
      op_b_d = (sel_ex_rs2 && !alu_src && !is_jump) ? ex_result
             : (is_jump ? 32'd4 : alu_src ? imm : rs2_early)
    i.e. still ONE late 2:1 mux on ex_result, replacement values in the
    early leg. EX loses the alu_src and is_auipc muxes in front of the
    adder/shifter and the `is_jump ? pc+4` mux behind the ALU (JAL/JALR
    already decode alu_op = ADD, so the link address is the ALU sum):
    ex_result = ALU output. rs1_val/rs2_val are kept unchanged for the
    branch compare, JALR target, AGU, store data, divider and RVFI.
(3) Multiplier and divider operands come straight from rs1_val/rs2_val
    (not through op_a/op_b); MUL stays single-cycle in EX as an arm of
    the ALU result mux (the proxy used `is_mul ? mul_out : alu_result`;
    keeping the four MUL arms inside the ALU case with separate ma/mb
    inputs is equivalent and saves a level).
Result in proxy A: worst paths are ~11.05 ns and balanced between
op_a/op_b flop -> adder -> result mux -> bypass mux -> operand register
(the DSP-absorbed copy, u_alu/mult_5_s1) and BSRAM read -> load align ->
MEM bypass -> ID/EX; nothing ends in dmem_* any more. Expected fitness
~156.7 x 90.5/71.3 = ~198 if the other two placement options follow
option 0; +22% claimed to leave room for median spread. Falsifiable:
`make timing` must show no dmem_* endpoint among the worst setup paths
and >= ~85 MHz on option 0, and CoreMark must still take 4,491,817
cycles. RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS: keep the MUL stand-ins as ALU arms on the
same operands the real multiplier uses (rs1_val/rs2_val) so both builds
stay consistent; decoder and invariants 2/3/10 untouched.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-002-r3s1 (improvement, +32.39%): New champion at 93.2 MHz with CoreMark unchanged at 4,491,817 cycles (2736 LUT / 613 FF, formal 53/53 first try): taking the dmem BSRAM address pins off the end of the ALU cone — a dedicated `rs1_val + imm` adder (the existing JALR-target adder, so no new carry chain) into its own EX/MEM.mem_addr register, plus ALU-only operands op_a/op_b captured in ID so EX has no alu_src/is_auipc mux before the adder and shifter and no `is_jump ? pc+4` mux after them — gave 89.2 MHz as written, and re-timing all three place options then removing the new worst path twice inside the slot gave the rest (shifter outputs OR-ed in after the op-select mux: 90.8; MEM bypass split into an early alu_result leg and a late load-data leg: 93.2, but option 0 fell 2.5 MHz on that step, so the last +2.4 MHz is one run and not shown to be outside placement noise); reusable: once a dedicated address adder makes the ALU result dead for LOAD/STORE/BRANCH, the operand selects only have to be right for OP, OP-IMM, LUI, AUIPC, JAL and JALR and collapse to raw opcode bits (`instr[2]` picks pc, `instr[6]` picks 4, `!instr[6] & instr[5] & !instr[2]` picks rs2), keeping the decoder's funct3/funct7 legality logic out of the bypass selects, and the local `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median reproduced the scored Fmax (93.175 MHz); the wall is now ~10.7 ns at ~73% routing in only 6 LUTs and is a near three-way tie — ID/EX.ctrl.alu_op (fanout 58) -> op decode -> ALU result -> ID bypass mux -> rs2_val_q, 0.23 ns behind it EX/MEM.mem_addr[1:0] -> load aligner -> ID mux -> DSP-absorbed operand register, and on option 0 op_b -> 32-bit carry chain -> ALU result -> ID mux -> DSP-absorbed operand register — so trimming LUT levels on one leg is worth at most ~0.23 ns (~2 MHz; untested example: one-hot ALU class selects registered in ID/EX), a scratch variant that also moved MUL to MEM was no faster (89.4 vs 90.5 MHz, option 0 only), and the next Fmax step must shorten the EX-result and load-data loops into ID together or cut their routing (each now fans out to four 32-bit ID mux legs: rs1_val, rs2_val, op_a, op_b).

title: Fetch-stage gshare + JAL predictor re-ported alone onto the 70 MHz bypass-at-decode champion (registered-select verify, EX/MEM training)
motivation:
The 156.68 champion still has no branch prediction (its CoreMark cycle
count is the unpredicted 4,491,817): every taken branch, JAL and JALR
resolved in EX kills the word in IF/ID and costs one fetch slot. The
BTB-less fetch predictor was built twice on older parents and both times
measured the same +7.2% iter/cycle (4,491,817 -> 4,189,486 cycles),
formal 53/53 first try, but lost its slot to a bigger same-round Fmax
sibling, so it is still absent from the champion.
An ISS branch trace of the timed region (10 iterations, 2,922,015
instructions) taken for this proposal sizes it exactly:
529,588 branches (294,425 taken), 49,367 JAL, 13,735 JALR (every one a
`ret`) = 357,527 lost fetch slots today. A 1024x2 gshare (idx =
pc[11:2]^ghr[9:0]) mispredicts 38,242 (7.2%), leaving 51,977 lost slots:
305,550 saved, matching the 302,331 cycles measured in r2s2 (a bubble is
~0.99 cycle). The same trace shows nothing bigger is left in this
category: a return stack would add only +0.33% (13.7K slots), a 4096x2
PHT +0.11%, plain bimodal is 0.03% worse, a perfect direction predictor
+0.9%. So the right predictor is the proven small one, and the whole
job is integrating it Fmax-neutrally: +7.2% clears the 4.6% bar only if
Fmax loses less than ~2.4% (1.7 MHz of 70.4).
The champion makes that plausible: its wall is the ~14.3 ns operand flop
-> MUL DSP / barrel shifter -> ALU result mux -> pc+4 mux -> EX/MEM ->
dmem address path, wrong-path kills already happen at the ID/EX sync
clear (id_bubble), and the branch compare starts from ID/EX operand
flops (no forwarding mux in EX), so the redirect path has slack and the
r2s2 verify structure removes logic from it rather than adding any.
(Side note for other categories: the trace also shows 203,959 load-use
bubbles, ~4.9% of cycles, untouched by this hypothesis.)

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add the proven BTB-less predictor to the fetch/decode cycle of the
champion and change nothing else.
Fetch side (imem is combinational and IF/ID is not a flop, so the raw
fetched word is available in the PC cycle): pred_taken =
(JAL | (legal BRANCH & pht_ctr[1])) & !imm[1], JALR never predicted.
Target is exact, pd_target = pc + (JAL ? imm_J : imm_B) from one adder,
so no BTB. PC update: redirect ? redirect_target : stall ? hold :
pred_taken ? pd_target : pc+4 (redirect still overrides stall; stall_if
already covers an undelivered word, so a garbage prediction during an
imem stall is ignored). PHT = 1024x2 LUT-RAM, async read at
pc[11:2] ^ ghr[9:0], one sync write port, no reset loop.
Verify in EX from registered selects only. ID/EX's sync-cleared control
group gains pred_taken, br_chk = is_branch & !imm[1], br_sel_lt =
funct3[2], br_unsigned = funct3[1], br_pol = funct3[0] ^ pred_taken and
jalr_static = is_jalr; pht_idx[9:0] / pht_ctr[1:0] ride in the data
group. EX computes eq and one signed/unsigned lt on the ID/EX operand
flops:
  redirect = (br_chk & ((br_sel_lt ? lt : eq) ^ br_pol))
           | (jalr_static & !jalr_lo[1])
  redirect_target = jalr ? jalr_sum&~1 : pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm
with every select a flop. No `valid &` is needed (a bubble clears all
enabling bits). A predicted JAL never redirects; a JAL or taken branch
with imm[1]=1 is never predicted, traps and falls through exactly as
today (misalign trap, pc_next and RVFI logic keep using the true
branch_taken, off the redirect net). This replaces the 6-way
branch_cond case + is_branch AND + misalign AND + is_jump OR, so the
redirect net gets shorter, and a mispredict is still exactly one bubble:
the change can only remove bubbles.
Training from the EX/MEM flop: pht_idx, pht_ctr, actual taken and
is_branch are captured in EX/MEM; the saturating-counter write and the
GHR shift happen the one cycle the branch sits in MEM (a branch is never
a mem op, so it is never held there and trains exactly once). The
comparator therefore never drives LUT-RAM write data.
Expected: 4,491,817 -> ~4,189,500 cycles (+7.2% iter/cycle) at ~70 MHz
-> fitness ~168. New paths are short in the timed netlist: PC/GHR flop
-> XOR -> LUT-RAM read -> 64:1 mux -> next-PC mux (~8-9 ns), and
imemData (a register in fpga/core_bench_si.sv) -> predecode/adder -> PC.
Implementation guard: after building, `make timing TARGET=bench` must
still list the ALU -> dmem address path as worst; if a predictor path
shows up instead, first drop the GHR XOR (bimodal index = pc[11:2],
training index from EX/MEM.pc, costs 0.03% IPC per the trace), then
carry the not-predicted target (pred_taken ? pc+4 : pd_target) from
fetch in ID/EX so redirect_target needs no EX adder.
Deliberately excluded: return-address stack (+0.33% for a 30-bit target
compare on the redirect net), larger or tournament PHTs (+0.1%).

changes.description: New module: 1024x2-bit gshare PHT pinned to distributed LUT-RAM (one async read port, one sync write port, no reset loop) + 10-bit GHR (reset 0). Lookup idx = pc[11:2] ^ ghr; update writes saturate(pht_ctr, taken) at the carried pht_idx and shifts the GHR on the same enable.

Add pred_taken, pht_idx[9:0], pht_ctr[1:0] to if_id_t and id_ex_t; add br_chk, br_sel_lt, br_unsigned, br_pol, jalr_static to id_ex_t; add pht_idx, pht_ctr to ex_mem_t (branch_taken and ctrl.is_branch already there) for training.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-003-r3s2 (regression, +0.67%): Unlike the two earlier predictor builds this one was not just out-raced by a sibling (157.73 vs r3s1's 207.43) — it barely beat its own 156.68 parent: the fetch-stage gshare + JAL predictor delivered its +7.2% IPC a third time (fitness x Fmax implies ~4.19M cycles vs 4,491,817; formal 53/53 first try, cosim pass) but Fmax fell 6.1% (70.4 -> 66.1 MHz scored median; option 0 71.3 -> 64.9) against a 6.7% break-even, and it fell without any predictor or redirect path becoming critical — all five worst paths were still imm_q/is_auipc -> alu_b mux -> MUL DSP -> ALU out mux -> ex_result -> dmem BSRAM address, just ~1.4 ns longer (a 9-cell instance at 20.68 ns arrival vs the parent's 10-cell 19.31 ns, 54% routing, so wire not logic) in a design grown 2509 -> 3138 LUT4 (+25%), +39 FF, +64 LUT-RAM — so the hypothesis's guard "the old ALU -> dmem path must still be worst" passed while the idea failed and its path-keyed fallbacks never fired: a block that adds no critical path still taxes a routing-dominated wall through area/placement (a cost that was invisible under the 199 ns and 26 ns walls of the first two builds), so "Fmax-neutral" must be gated on the `--all-options` Fmax number against the parent, never on the identity of the worst path, with area-cutting rather than path-cutting fallbacks ready; the predictor is still absent from the 93.2 MHz champion (still 4,491,817 cycles), whose ~10.7 ns wall is ~73% routing and therefore probably more area-sensitive, where +7.2% IPC again breaks even at -6.7% Fmax (~6 MHz), so a re-port should start from a lean variant and time it before growing it (all untested: 256x2 PHT = 16 LUT-RAM with a 16:1 instead of 64:1 read mux, bimodal pc[11:2] index trained from EX/MEM.pc, which the ISS trace prices at only -0.03% IPC and which drops the GHR and the pht_idx pipeline flops, and carrying the not-predicted target from fetch in ID/EX so EX loses the pc+imm adder and 3:1 target mux; a PHT-free JAL-only version is worth just ~1.1% = 49,367 slots, so the direction PHT is where the gain is); practical: on this nret=1 core plain `make formal TARGET=bench` / `make cosim TARGET=bench` pick the dual-channel setup and fail, the passing gates are `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh` and `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`, and this slot lost a gate cycle rediscovering that and ended with a single option-0 timing run and no time to try a fallback.

title: Shrink the late EX->ID loops: one shared 33x33 signed multiplier (1 DSP site instead of 3) plus pre-decoded one-hot ALU / load-lane selects
motivation:
The 93.2 MHz champion's wall is ~10.7 ns at ~73% routing in only 6 LUT
levels, a three-way tie that always ends at the ID bypass mux:
(1) ID/EX.ctrl.alu_op (fanout 58) -> op decode -> ALU result -> ID mux -> rs2_val_q
(2) EX/MEM.mem_addr[1:0] -> load aligner -> ID mux -> DSP-absorbed operand reg
(3) op_b -> 32-bit carry chain -> ALU result -> ID mux -> DSP-absorbed operand reg
The logged worst path is exactly (3): u_id/op_b_q_0 -> ... -> u_alu/mul_ss_63_s0,
i.e. the endpoint is a multiplier input register. alu.sv instantiates THREE
full 32x32 products (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su; the log shows dsp: 6 = three
MULT36X36), and Gowin absorbs a copy of rs1_val_q/rs2_val_q into each. So
every bit of the latest signal in the design (ex_result / load data ->
ID bypass mux) must be routed to three fixed DSP sites spread along the
DSP row plus the fabric flops, and the ALU/ID-mux cluster is pulled
toward the centroid of three DSPs. With routing at 73% of the wall this
endpoint fan-out is the cheapest thing to remove; r3s0 already measured
1.76 ns of route into a DSP column on this same endpoint. No stall or
bubble is added, so CoreMark must stay at exactly 4,491,817 cycles; the
whole gain has to be Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Step 1 (primary, always build): replace the three 32x32 multipliers by
ONE 33x33 signed multiplier. The 33rd operand bits are registered in
ID/EX next to rs1_val_q/rs2_val_q, in the same hold-only data always_ff
(same reset/CE so the DSP still absorbs the whole 33-bit operand):
  mul_a_hi_q <= rs1_val_d[31] & !(instr[13] & instr[12]);  // MULH, MULHSU signed a
  mul_b_hi_q <= rs2_val_d[31] & !instr[13];                // MULH signed b
(raw funct3 bits, don't-care for MUL low half and for non-MUL words, so
no decoder logic enters the bypass path). alu.sv computes
prod = $signed({ma_hi,ma}) * $signed({mb_hi,mb}); MUL = prod[31:0],
MULH/MULHSU/MULHU = prod[63:32], so mul_r shrinks from a 4:1 mux over
three DSP outputs to a 2:1 hi/lo select. Result: 6 -> 2 DSP blocks, the
late bypass-mux outputs drive one DSP site instead of three, and the
placer can pull the ALU and ID mux next to that one site. The
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS stand-ins keep using the 32-bit ma/mb unchanged.
Step 2 (same theme, keep only if the --all-options median improves):
remove the binary control decode from the same loops by registering
one-hot selects a stage early. ID/EX gets ALU arm selects decoded in ID
(in the bubble-cleared ctrl group): sel_addsub, do_sub, sel_slt,
sel_sltu, a 2-bit logic function (AND/OR/XOR/pass-b for LUI), sel_sll,
sel_sr, sr_arith, sel_mul_lo, sel_mul_hi, sel_div. alu.sv then uses ONE
33-bit add/sub chain for ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU (instead of separate a+b, a-b
and two compare chains), one LUT4 per bit for the logic arm, and a flat
select-gated AND-OR with adder and shifters as last-arriving inputs, so
the alu_op compare/case level and its fanout-58 net leave leg (1) and
(3) and the ALU gets smaller.
Step 3 (optional, same gate): EX/MEM gets load-lane selects decoded in
EX from the existing 2-bit (rs1[1:0]+imm[1:0]) sum, mem_width and
mem_sext, so the MEM aligner is a one-hot lane mux plus one sign-fill
level off dmem_rdata instead of a variable shift followed by a width
case (leg 2).
Expected: step 1 alone ~+3-5 MHz from routing relief on two of the three
tied legs, steps 2-3 ~0.3-0.5 ns of logic on the remaining ones:
~98-101 MHz at unchanged cycles (+5..8%). Accept or reject each step on
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median vs the
93.175 MHz parent (never option 0 alone, never worst-path identity).
Gates on this nret=1 core: `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash
formal/run_all.sh` and `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`. Risks: Gowin
may refuse to absorb the 33-bit operand registers if the hi-bit flops
differ in reset/CE from rs?_val_q (check the DSP count is 2 and the
path endpoint is still a DSP register, else the MUL path grows); the
gain is routing-driven and unmeasured, hence low confidence.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-001-r4s0 (regression, +1.30%): "Regression" only means it lost the round to sibling hyp-20261124-002-r4s1 (210.12 vs 227.15) — against the 207.43 parent, replacing the three 32x32 products by ONE 33x33 signed multiplier (33rd operand bits `rs1[31] & !(f3[1] & f3[0])` / `rs2[31] & !f3[1]` registered beside rs1_val_q/rs2_val_q in the same reset/CE block, MUL = prod[31:0], MULH/MULHSU/MULHU = prod[63:32]) was correct first try (formal 53/53, cosim pass, fitness ratio = Fmax ratio so still 4,491,817 cycles) and Gowin did absorb the 33-bit operand registers (DSP 6 -> 2, 2736 -> 2605 LUT4), but it bought only 93.175 -> 94.38 MHz (~0.14 ns of the ~10.7 ns wall; one run per option, option 0 at 90.95, so not shown to be outside placement noise) instead of the predicted +3-5 MHz: the fan-out of the late ID bypass mux to three DSP sites was not what the routing-dominated wall was paying for — the worst path still ends in the one remaining DSP-absorbed operand register (op_b_q -> 32-bit carry chain -> ALU -> ID mux -> u_alu/mul_p) and the tie is wider than the three legs the hypothesis listed, the second-worst path being imem word (the LFSR register in the timed netlist) -> regfile read -> ID bypass mux -> rs1_val_q in 9 cells with no EX logic in it at all; the scratch-only step 2 (ALU arm selects pre-decoded one-hot into ID/EX, one shared 33-bit add/sub/compare chain, flat select-gated AND-OR result; formal 53/53, cosim not run, never shipped) confirmed it by making Fmax WORSE, 94.38 -> 91.79 MHz, despite -172 LUT4 (2433), +13 FF and 11 -> 9 logic levels, its worst paths becoming imem word -> regfile/ID -> DSP operand register and dmem BSRAM -> load aligner -> ID mux -> DSP operand register — so on this wall neither fewer ALU logic levels, nor a smaller EX, nor fewer DSP sinks is a lever: every leg converges on the ID bypass mux and its DSP-absorbed rs1_val/rs2_val endpoint, shortening the ALU leg only hands the wall to the regfile-read and load-data legs at the same ~10.6-10.9 ns, and EX-side edits worth hundreds of LUTs move the median by only +1.2 / -2.6 MHz, less than the option-0 vs option-1/2 gap of the same build (3.4 and 4.3 MHz here), so a predicted ~3% micro-opt cannot be accepted or rejected from one `--all-options` run and the alu_op one-hot idea floated in the r3s1 lesson is now tested and negative; the next Fmax idea has to shorten what all legs share (the bypass mux -> DSP-absorbed operand register endpoint, or the regfile-read and load-data legs together — step 3's one-hot load-lane selects were never built, untested) rather than any single EX leg, and since the new champion's alu.sv still holds mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su (6 DSP) the single-multiplier edit remains a cheap IPC-neutral port worth -131 LUT4 / -4 DSP of area, with no Fmax claim attached.

title: Zero-bubble redirects: EX-resolved target drives the fetch address in the same cycle
motivation:
The champion (93.2 MHz, 4,491,817 CoreMark cycles) still pays one ID/EX
bubble for EVERY taken branch, JAL and JALR: redirect is resolved in EX,
written into the PC register, and the target is only fetched the cycle
after, while the wrong-path word sitting in IF is killed. Three predictor
builds showed that removing only the predictable part of those bubbles is
worth +7.2% IPC, but each paid for it with a PHT, GHR, predecode adder and
verify logic (+630 LUT4), and the last one lost 6.1% Fmax to pure
area/routing pressure. The bubble itself is structural, not fundamental:
imem is read combinationally and there is no IF/ID flop, so IF+ID are one
cycle. If the fetch ADDRESS (not the PC register) is muxed with the EX
redirect target, the target instruction is fetched, decoded, bypassed and
captured into ID/EX in the very cycle the branch resolves. Every redirect
then costs 0 bubbles - the IPC of a perfect predictor (all taken branches
and all jumps, not just the gshare-predictable ones) with no predictor
state at all, ~+30 LUT instead of +630, and `redirect` REMOVED from the
ID/EX synchronous-clear cone.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion (93.2 MHz, 4,491,817 CoreMark cycles) still pays one ID/EX
bubble for EVERY taken branch, JAL and JALR: redirect is resolved in EX,

and all jumps, not just the gshare-predictable ones) with no predictor
