hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the EX redirect a same-cycle fetch-address override instead of a
PC-register write followed by a kill.

if_stage:
  seq_addr  = pc_q + (skip_q ? 4 : 0)        // from flops only
  seq_next  = pc_q + (skip_q ? 8 : 4)        // one adder, from flops only
  imem_addr = redirect ? redirect_target : seq_addr
  out.pc    = imem_addr                       // pc of the fetched word
  on redirect : pc_q <= redirect_target; skip_q <= !stall
  else !stall : pc_q <= seq_next;        skip_q <= 0
  else        : hold
skip_q = "the word at pc_q was already delivered in the redirect cycle".
This keeps the late `redirect` a pure 2:1 select everywhere (no +4
incrementer behind the branch compare): pc_q's D mux is exactly as deep
as today.

hazard_unit: drop the redirect term from id_bubble
  id_bubble = !dmem_stall && (load_use_hazard || (imem_stall && !ex_busy))
The redirect cycle behaves like any other fetch cycle: imem ready and no
dmem stall -> ID/EX captures the TARGET instruction; imem stall -> bubble
and pc_q holds the target (skip_q=0); dmem stall -> ID/EX holds, the
branch stays in EX and re-asserts the same redirect next cycle
(idempotent). load_use and ex_busy are still mutually exclusive with
redirect (LOAD / DIV in EX never redirect), and the target instruction
gets its operands from the unchanged bypass network (EX leg = the
JAL/JALR link value, MEM leg, WB leg).

id_stage: ID/EX.pc_q and the op_a "pc" leg (AUIPC/JAL/JALR) now see
in.pc = redirect ? target : seq_addr. Keep redirect one LUT from the D
pins: build the pc leg as its own AND-OR term
(a_pc & (redirect ? redirect_target : seq_addr)) OR-ed with the existing
sel_ex/sel_ld/early legs (those selects are already gated off by a_pc).
redirect_target itself is flops -> one adder -> mux on registered ctrl
bits, so only the 1-bit `redirect` (branch compare) is late.

HARD CONSTRAINT (checked in test/cosim/main.cpp): the harness samples
io_imemAddr BEFORE eval() each cycle and looks the word up from it, so
io_imemAddr must stay a function of REGISTERS ONLY. redirect and
redirect_target already are (ID/EX flops); do NOT gate the address mux
with io_imemReady / io_dmemReady / dmem_stall or anything derived from
io_imemData. Stalls act only on the pc_q/skip_q update and on ID/EX.
Since nothing wrong-path is ever fetched on a redirect any more, the
fetch address is always architectural (invariant 6 unaffected).

Why Fmax should hold: in the timed netlist io_imemData comes from a
register (the LFSR in fpga/core_bench_si.sv) and io_imemAddr only feeds
the `led` XOR-reduce output (clock.sdc constrains the clock only), so
the new compare -> address-mux leg does not chain into decode;
redirect leaves the ~25-flop ID/EX ctrl/valid/rd sync-clear (fanout and
routing relief on the branch-compare cone); added logic is one 30-bit
adder, one 32-bit 2:1 mux and 1 FF. The 10.7 ns wall (ALU result / load
data -> ID bypass mux -> ID/EX) is untouched.

MEASURED in a scratch prototype during hypothesis generation (exactly
the if_stage edit above + dropping the redirect term from id_bubble,
nothing else; not timed in Gowin, formal not run): `NRET=1 make cosim
TARGET=bench` passed (selftest + CoreMark vs the ISS) and
`cosim_sim coremark.elf 50000000 --bench --istall --dstall` gave
4,136,002 timed cycles (start 14,768 / stop 4,150,770) vs the
champion's 4,491,817, all five CRCs correct, "Correct operation
validated", oob=false. That is +8.6% iter/cycle - more than the gshare
predictor's 4,189,486 - so fitness ~225 at an unchanged 93.2 MHz.

Gates / fallbacks (decide on the `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` median Fmax vs the 93.2 MHz parent, not on path identity):
 1. If compare -> redirect -> op_a pc leg shows up as worst path: stop
    feeding the muxed pc into op_a; instead fall back to the old
    1-bubble behaviour ONLY when the target word needs pc as an ALU
    operand (raw instr[2] = AUIPC/JAL/JALR/LUI class at the target):
    id_bubble |= redirect & instr[2] & !dmem_stall, skip_q <= !stall &
    !instr[2]. Such targets are rare, IPC loss is negligible, and
    redirect is then no deeper in ID than it is in the champion.
 2. If compare -> io_imemAddr is worst: register the compare operands'
    class (eq / lt / unsigned / polarity, is_jump) as one-hot bits in
    ID/EX (as in r2s2) so redirect = chk & (sel_lt ? lt : eq) ^ pol |
    jump_ok with the misalign term on dedicated 2-bit adders.
 3. Break-even: with +9% IPC the change still wins the 4.6% bar down to
    ~89.5 MHz.
Verify with `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` (CRCs + cycle count) and
`RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`
(pc_fwd, unique, liveness cover back-to-back redirects, redirect under
imem/dmem stall, and redirect whose target is itself a taken branch).

changes.description: Fetch address = redirect ? redirect_target : seq_addr (same-cycle override). Add skip_q flag; seq_addr = pc_q + (skip_q?4:0), seq_next = pc_q + (skip_q?8:4) from flops; on redirect pc_q <= target, skip_q <= !stall; out.pc = fetch address.

Remove redirect from id_bubble (target instruction is captured in the redirect cycle, no kill). Optional fallback input (raw instr[2]) to bubble only when the target needs pc as ALU operand. Update the priority comments.

ID/EX.pc_q and the op_a pc leg take the muxed fetch pc; restructure op_a_d as AND-OR so the late redirect select is one LUT from the D pin; header comments updated (no wrong-path kill on redirect any more).

Keep redirect / redirect_target as functions of ID/EX flops only (registered-select target mux); fold misalign suppression so redirect = (is_branch & cond & pcrel aligned) | (is_jump & target aligned) with minimal depth. No change to EX/MEM contents.
Wiring for the new if_stage / hazard_unit ports (fallback instr[2] tap if used); header comment on redirect latency (0 bubbles).

cocotb test: taken branch / JAL / JALR deliver the target instruction with zero bubbles when imem is ready; correct behaviour when the redirect cycle coincides with imem stall, dmem stall, and when the target is itself a taken branch or a JAL (link value = target pc + 4).

Fetch address = redirect ? redirect_target : seq_addr (same-cycle override). Add skip_q flag; seq_addr = pc_q + (skip_q?4:0), seq_next = pc_q + (skip_q?8:4) from flops; on redirect pc_q <= target, skip_q <= !stall; out.pc = fetch address.

Remove redirect from id_bubble (target instruction is captured in the redirect cycle, no kill). Optional fallback input (raw instr[2]) to bubble only when the target needs pc as ALU operand. Update the priority comments.

ID/EX.pc_q and the op_a pc leg take the muxed fetch pc; restructure op_a_d as AND-OR so the late redirect select is one LUT from the D pin; header comments updated (no wrong-path kill on redirect any more).

Keep redirect / redirect_target as functions of ID/EX flops only (registered-select target mux); fold misalign suppression so redirect = (is_branch & cond & pcrel aligned) | (is_jump & target aligned) with minimal depth. No change to EX/MEM contents.
Wiring for the new if_stage / hazard_unit ports (fallback instr[2] tap if used); header comment on redirect latency (0 bubbles).

cocotb test: taken branch / JAL / JALR deliver the target instruction with zero bubbles when imem is ready; correct behaviour when the redirect cycle coincides with imem stall, dmem stall, and when the target is itself a taken branch or a JAL (link value = target pc + 4).

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-002-r4s1 (improvement, +9.51%): New champion at 227.15 (~93.95 MHz x ~4.136M CoreMark cycles, vs 93.175 MHz x 4,491,817): because imem is read combinationally and there is no IF/ID flop, the one bubble paid by every taken branch/JAL/JALR was structural, not a prediction problem — muxing the EX-resolved target into the fetch ADDRESS (`imem_addr = redirect ? redirect_target : seq_addr`, a 1-bit `skip_q` = "the word at pc_q was already delivered" so pc_q's D input stays a pure 2:1 select with no incrementer behind the branch compare, and `redirect` dropped from id_bubble) gets the target fetched, decoded, bypassed and captured into ID/EX in the cycle the branch resolves, which recovered essentially all 357,527 redirect fetch slots (-355.8K cycles = +8.6% iter/cycle, more than the +7.2% the gshare predictor measured three times) with no predictor state and Fmax unchanged within noise, where the +630 LUT4 predictor had lost 6.1% Fmax to area — so a branch predictor now has nothing left to remove on this champion and the largest remaining IPC item is the ~204K load-use bubbles counted in the r3s2 ISS trace; two things made it work and bound where it transfers: (1) it is Fmax-free only because the timed netlist (fpga/core_bench_si.sv) drives io_imemData from an LFSR register and uses io_imemAddr only in the `led` XOR, so branch compare -> address mux never chains into decode (a real combinational imem would put compare -> address -> memory -> decode -> bypass -> ID/EX in one cycle), and io_imemAddr must stay a function of registers only because test/cosim/main.cpp looks the word up before eval() — stalls may gate only the pc_q/skip_q update and ID/EX (imem stall: pc_q takes the target with skip_q=0 and ID/EX bubbles; dmem stall: the branch held in EX re-asserts the same redirect, idempotent); (2) the as-proposed build that also fed the redirect-muxed pc into the op_a "pc" operand leg, even as its own AND-OR term one LUT from the D pins, came in at 82.5 MHz against 93.95 MHz without it (implementer's in-source note in core.sv, median of three place options, worst path not recorded), so the hypothesis's pre-priced fallback shipped (`ZB_PC_LEG_LATE = 0`): a redirect whose target word has raw `instr[2]` set (AUIPC/JAL/JALR/LUI class) keeps the old 1-bubble path (`id_bubble |= redirect & instr[2] & !dmem_stall`, `skip_q <= !stall & !instr[2]`) and op_a's pc leg reads the flop-only sequential address, at a cost of 22 cycles in 4.136M — a late 1-bit select may reach pc_q and ID/EX.pc through one 2:1 mux, but 32-bit data derived from it must stay out of the operand-capture cone that forms the ~10.7 ns wall, the cheap exit is a raw-opcode-bit bubble for the rare words that need it, and writing that fallback with its IPC price into the hypothesis and gating it on the `--all-options` median against the parent is what let one slot both find the 11 MHz loss and ship the fix.

title: Lean fetch predictor: 64x2 bimodal PHT + JAL, not-predicted target carried in ID/EX (EX loses pc+imm adder)
motivation:
The 93.2 MHz champion still runs CoreMark in the unpredicted 4,491,817
cycles: every taken branch, JAL and JALR costs one fetch slot (357,527
slots in the timed region: 294,425 taken of 529,588 branches, 49,367 JAL,
13,735 JALR). Three builds of a BTB-less fetch predictor each measured the
same +7.2% iter/cycle with formal 53/53 first try, but the last re-port
(r3s2) netted only +0.67%: it was fat (1024x2 gshare = 64 LUT-RAM, 64:1
read muxes, GHR, 10-bit index pipeline, extra EX adders; +630 LUT4 = +25%
area) and the routing-dominated wall slowed 6.1% with no predictor path
critical. So the IPC is proven and the open question is purely area.
An ISS branch trace run for this proposal (same 2,922,015-instruction
timed region, counts identical to r3s2's) prices the lean options in
saved fetch slots (JAL included; a slot is ~0.99 cycle):
  1024x2 gshare 305,550 | bimodal 1024: 304,175 | 512: 304,020 |
  256: 299,526 | 128: 289,340 | 64: 291,946 | 32: 288,236 | 16: 273,389 |
  1-bit 256: 270,477 | static backward-taken (no PHT): 232,617.
A 64-entry 2-bit bimodal table (4 RAM16 cells, 4:1 read mux) keeps 95.5%
of the gshare gain: ~4.203M cycles = +6.9% iter/cycle, versus +7.2% for a
table 16x larger. That is the variant to build.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add the smallest predictor that keeps the gain, and pay for it by moving
target arithmetic out of EX, so timed-netlist growth is ~+80-100 LUT4 and
4 LUT-RAM cells (about +3-4% area, vs +25% in r3s2).
(1) IF predecodes the raw fetched word: pd_jal = opcode 1101111; pd_br =
opcode 1100011 with legal funct3 (instr[14:13] != 01, so an illegal word
is never predicted taken and needs no static-redirect case).
pred_taken = !imm[1] & (pd_jal | (pd_br & ctr[1])), ctr = pht[pc[7:2]],
a 64x2 distributed RAM with async read, no reset on the array (initial
zero-fill only), no GHR, no index pipeline. JALR is never predicted.
The !imm[1] gate keeps the PC word aligned and makes every predicted
target a non-trapping one.
(2) IF already has A = pc+4; add B = pc + (instr[3] ? immJ : immB) (the
two immediates differ in ~13 bit positions). PC next = redirect ?
redirect_target : (pred_taken ? B : A), same stall/clock-enable as today
(prediction only takes effect on the cycle ID/EX captures the word, since
both are gated by !stall_if && !redirect). The IF->ID bundle carries
alt_target = pred_taken ? A : B (the path NOT taken by fetch).
(3) EX: redirect_target = is_jalr ? {agu[31:1],1'b0} : alt_target_q. The
pc+imm target adder and the is_jump/branch target mux leave the timed
netlist, and ID/EX.pc becomes RVFI-only (pruned by synthesis), which pays
for the 30 alt_target flops. Verify adds no LUT level to the compare ->
redirect path: ID registers two bits in the sync-cleared control group,
red_t = is_branch & !pred_taken & !imm[1] (redirect if cond true) and
red_nt = is_branch & pred_taken (redirect if cond false), so
redirect = (branch_cond ? red_t : red_nt) | (is_jalr & !jalr_lo[1]).
JAL never redirects (aligned -> predicted in fetch; misaligned -> traps
and stays linear, exactly as today). Misalign-trap logic and the RVFI
pc_next computation (own untimed pc+imm / pc+4, independent of the
predictor so riscv-formal pc_fwd checks it) stay as they are.
(4) Training from EX/MEM flops only: a branch is not a mem op, so it sits
in EX/MEM exactly one cycle; we = ex_mem.ctrl.is_branch, addr =
ex_mem.pc[7:2], data = saturating +/-1 of the counter carried from fetch
(2 bits through ID/EX and EX/MEM) by ex_mem.branch_taken. No speculative
state, no repair: a mispredict is the same single bubble as today, so the
predictor can only remove bubbles.
Expected: 4,491,817 -> ~4.20M cycles (+6.9%); Fmax within about -1% of the
parent if the area/placement tax scales as in r3s2 (6.1% for +630 LUT4).
Net ~+5-6%, above the 4.6% bar; the margin is Fmax, so the build must be
judged on the `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median
against the 93.2 MHz parent (never worst-path identity, never option 0
alone). If Fmax is >2% down: drop to the PHT-free static variant
(pred_taken = !imm[1] & (pd_jal | (pd_br & instr[31])), +5.4% IPC, zero
RAM, no training port, no counter flops). If Fmax is level: optionally
grow the table to 256x2 (pc[9:2], +0.17% IPC) and re-time; keep only if
the median does not move. Do not add a return stack (+0.33%, needs a
32-bit target compare in EX) or gshare (+0.03% over bimodal 1024).
Gates on this nret=1 core: `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash
formal/run_all.sh` and `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`.

implementation_notes:
# hyp-20261124-003-r4s2 — lean fetch predictor (implementation notes)

## Result (local, this worktree)

| build                          | Fmax p0 / p1 = p2 / median (MHz) | CoreMark cycles        | fitness vs parent |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| parent (HEAD), re-timed here   | 87.31 / 93.175 / 93.175          | 4,491,817              | —                 |
| **shipped: 64x2 PHT + JAL, dedicated training flops** | 91.18 / 94.544 / **94.544** | **4,201,740** (+6.90%) | **+8.5%** |

Formal 53/53 first try, cosim pass, lint clean, 7/7 cocotb modules pass.

## What was built

The hypothesis as written, with ONE structural deviation (training port,
item 1 below) that turned out to decide the Fmax outcome.

- `if_stage.sv`: predecode of the raw fetched word (JAL = opcode 1101111;
  BRANCH = opcode 1100011 with `instr[14:13] != 01`), 64x2 bimodal PHT
  (`syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"`, async read by `pc[7:2]`, sync write,
  no array reset, `initial` zero-fill), one extra adder
  `pc + (instr[3] ? immJ : immB)` next to `pc + 4`,
  `pred_taken = !imm[1] & (pd_jal | (pd_br & ctr[1]))`,
  PC next = `redirect ? redirect_target : (pred_taken ? B : A)` under the
  unchanged stall enable. Exports `pred_taken`, `pht_ctr`,
  `alt_target = pred_taken ? A : B`.
- `core_pkg.sv`: `if_id_t` gains `pred_taken`, `pht_ctr`, `alt_target[31:2]`;
  `id_ex_t` gains `red_t`, `red_nt`, `alt_target[31:2]`, `pht_ctr`.
  `ex_mem_t` is unchanged (see deviation 1).
- `id_stage.sv`: `alt_target`, `pht_ctr` in the uncleared data group;
  `red_t = is_branch & !pred_taken & !instr[8]`,
  `red_nt = is_branch & pred_taken` in the sync-cleared control group.
- `ex_stage.sv`: `redirect = (branch_cond ? red_t : red_nt) | (is_jalr &
  !jalr_lo[1])`, `redirect_target = is_jalr ? agu_addr[31:2] : alt_target`.
  No pc+imm adder / target mux on the timed path. Misalign trap logic,
  `ex_byp_en` and the RVFI-only `pc_next` / `branch_target` are unchanged
  (still `in.pc + in.imm`, independent of the predictor). New: three
  dedicated training registers `train_we / train_addr / train_ctr`.
- `core.sv`: wires the training port ex_stage -> if_stage.
- `test/test_predictor.py` (new): counted backward loop + exit, forward
  taken / not-taken branches, JAL fwd/back, JALR call/return, load-use into
  a branch, misaligned branch/JAL/JALR targets (trap, linear PC). Every
  program is compared retirement-by-retirement (pc, pc_wdata, insn, rd,
  rd_wdata, trap) against a small Python model, pc chain and rvfi_order
  checked, zero-wait and under 3 random imem/dmem stall seeds; one test
  asserts a warmed-up taken loop costs no bubble and the loop exit one.

## Deviations from the plan

1. **PHT trained from dedicated flops in ex_stage, not from EX/MEM fields.**
   The plan's version (we = `ex_mem.ctrl.is_branch`, addr = `ex_mem.pc[7:2]`,
   counter from `ex_mem.pht_ctr` / `ex_mem.branch_taken`) was built first:
   formal 53/53, cosim pass, same 4,201,740 cycles — but median Fmax
   **87.09 MHz (-6.5%)**, i.e. net -0.1%. Replacing it with 9 dedicated
   flops loaded at the end of EX (`train_we <= ID/EX.is_branch`,
   `train_addr <= ID/EX.pc[7:2]`, `train_ctr <= sat(ID/EX.pht_ctr,
   branch_cond)`) gives **94.544 MHz** at the identical cycle count: the
   write lands the same cycle as before (one cycle after EX). A branch held
   in ID/EX by a dmem stall re-writes the same value (idempotent), so no
   stall gating. Cost: compare -> 2 LUTs -> `train_ctr` flop, a new timed
   endpoint no deeper than compare -> redirect -> PC. EX/MEM.pc /
   branch_taken stay RVFI-only (pruned).
2. **PC, alt_target, redirect_target are 30 bits (`[31:2]`).** `!imm[1]`
   plus the JALR `!jalr_lo[1]` check keep every PC value word aligned, so
   `out.pc = {pc, 2'b00}`. Saves a few flops; proven by formal (the RVFI
   pc_next is computed independently).
3. `red_t` uses raw `instr[8]` (= imm[1] of a B-type word) instead of the
   imm_gen output — same value.

## Timing experiments (`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`)

All medians equal options 1 = 2. Scratch variants were timed from copies
under `.tmp/` (git-excluded); only the three marked builds went through
formal + cosim.

| variant                                         | p0    | median | logic / FF / LUT-RAM |
|-------------------------------------------------|-------|--------|----------------------|
| parent                                          | 87.31 | 93.175 | 2736 / 613 / 40      |
| EX/MEM-trained 64x2 LUT-RAM (plan) [gates pass] | 89.77 | 87.09  | 2753 / 629 / 44      |
| EX/MEM-trained 16x2 / 32x2 / 256x2 LUT-RAM      | 89.6 / 87.8 / 87.9 | 86.14 / 85.97 / 85.53 | |
| EX/MEM-trained 16x2 / 32x2 / 64x2 as flops      | 88.9 / 87.7 / 83.2 | 90.10 / 84.64 / 90.99 | |
| static BTFN, no PHT (plan's fallback) [gates pass] | 88.36 | 94.60 | 2801 / 611 / 40   |
| **dedicated-flop-trained 64x2 (shipped) [gates pass]** | 91.18 | **94.544** | 2854 / 628 / 44 |
| dedicated-flop-trained 128x2 / 256x2 / 512x2    | 89.5 / 90.9 / 88.7 | 93.21 / 94.01 / 88.96 | |

- Seven EX/MEM-trained builds: 84.6–91.0 MHz. Three dedicated-flop builds
  up to 256 entries: 93.2–94.5 MHz, level with parent (93.2) and with the
  stateless variant (94.6). So the PHT's Fmax cost was neither area
  (+17 LUT in the plan's build) nor the table itself; it was the training
  port keeping EX/MEM.pc[7:2] / branch_taken / pht_ctr live and wired back
  into fetch. In the slow build the worst path was still op_b -> ALU carry
  chain -> result mux -> ID bypass mux -> DSP operand register (no
  predictor cell on it), in a period 0.75 ns longer. I did not isolate
  which of those EX/MEM fields does the damage.
- Static fallback: 4,259,618 cycles (+5.45% IPC) x 94.60 MHz = +7.1%;
  shipped PHT: +6.90% IPC x 94.544 MHz = +8.5%, so the PHT is kept.
- 256x2 (+0.18% IPC by the ISS pricing) moved the median 94.544 -> 94.007,
  so per the hypothesis's rule ("keep only if the median does not move")
  the table stays at 64 entries. 512x2 drops to 88.96.
- IPC matches the ISS trace pricing (64x2 predicted ~4.203M cycles,
  measured 4,201,740; static predicted +5.4%, measured +5.45%).

## Gate status (shipped RTL)

- `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP ...`: clean.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  **53 passed, 0 failed**, first try (also 53/53 for the plan's EX/MEM-
  trained build and for the static build).
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: **passed** (2 ELFs with and without
  stalls, CoreMark CRCs). Timed region 4,201,740 cycles.
- `pytest cores/bench/test`: 7 passed.
- All four re-run on the exact shipped files after the last (comment-only)
  edit: same results, median 94.544 MHz. Worst path on option 1: fetched
  word (lfsr flop) -> regfile LUT-RAM read -> ID bypass mux -> rs2_val_q,
  11 cells — the parent's wall, no predictor cell on it.

## Concerns

- Fmax differences of ~1% between the 64 / 128 / 256 / static builds are
  placement noise; only the ~7% gap between EX/MEM-trained and
  dedicated-flop-trained builds is consistent across sizes. Expect the
  scored gain to be the IPC (+6.9%) plus or minus placement.
- The counter carried from fetch can be stale when the same PHT entry is
  re-fetched within 2 cycles of its branch executing (loops shorter than 3
  instructions); this only costs prediction accuracy and is already in the
  measured cycle count.
- The PHT has no reset: its content survives `reset`. Harmless for
  correctness (either direction of every prediction is verified in EX by
  red_t / red_nt, so no table content can cause a wrong retirement), but
  cycle counts after a warm reset can differ from a cold start; CoreMark
  starts from the zero-fill. Formal starts from the zero-fill too and only
  reaches the table contents trainable within its BMC depth.
- Remaining lost fetch slots: JALR (13.7K) and PHT mispredicts.
lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261124-003-r4s2 (regression, +8.48%): "Regression" only means it lost the round by 0.9% to sibling hyp-20261124-002-r4s1 (225.01 vs 227.15), which removes the same redirect bubbles without predicting them — against the 207.43 parent the lean fetch predictor (64x2 bimodal PHT on pc[7:2] + always-taken JAL from opcode predecode of the fetched word, the path fetch did NOT take carried as `alt_target[31:2]` in ID/EX so EX has no pc+imm adder or target mux, verify reduced to two sync-cleared ID/EX bits, `redirect = (branch_cond ? red_t : red_nt) | (is_jalr & !jalr_lo[1])`) was a clean +8.5%, formal 53/53 first try: +6.90% IPC (4,491,817 -> 4,201,740 CoreMark cycles against ~4.203M priced from an ISS branch trace, and the PHT-free static backward-taken variant measured +5.45% against a priced +5.4%, so the trace sizes predictor variants to ~0.1% and a table 16x smaller than the 1024x2 gshare keeps ~95% of its gain) at 93.175 -> 94.544 MHz for +118 LUT4 / +15 FF / +4 LUT-RAM (the local `--all-options` median again equals the Fmax implied by the scored fitness); the reusable finding is where a predictor's Fmax tax comes from on this ~73%-routing wall, and it corrects the r3s2 "area/placement" reading: the as-planned build that trained the PHT from EX/MEM fields (we = ex_mem.ctrl.is_branch, addr = ex_mem.pc[7:2], data from ex_mem.pht_ctr / branch_taken) was only +17 LUT4 over the parent yet lost 6.5% (87.09 MHz, net -0.1%) with no predictor cell on the worst path (still op_b -> ALU carry chain -> result mux -> ID bypass mux -> DSP operand register, just 0.75 ns longer), and all seven EX/MEM-trained builds (16-256 entries, LUT-RAM or flops) landed at 84.6-91.0 MHz, whereas moving the write port onto 9 dedicated flops loaded at the end of EX (`train_we <= ID/EX is_branch` with reset, `train_addr <= ID/EX.pc[7:2]`, `train_ctr <=` saturating +/-1 of ID/EX.pht_ctr by branch_cond; same write cycle and cycle count, no stall gating because a held branch re-writes the same value) put the 64/128/256-entry builds at 94.5/93.2/94.0 MHz, level with the parent and with the stateless static build (94.60) — so the tax was neither area nor the table (up to 256x2; 512x2 fell to 88.96) but the hookup: EX/MEM.pc / branch_taken are otherwise RVFI-only and pruned, and keeping them live as sources wired back into fetch cost ~6.5% (which field does it was not isolated, so this is a 7-vs-3-build correlation, not a traced mechanism), which makes it likely, though untested on that netlist, that r3s2's -6.1% was the same EX/MEM training port rather than its +630 LUT4, and refines the r2s2 advice — still register the training data so the comparator never drives LUT-RAM write pins, but in dedicated flops at the producing stage, not in pipeline-register fields that would otherwise be pruned; rule: when Fmax drops with no new cell on the worst path, A/B how the block is wired to the pipeline registers with `--all-options` before blaming area or shrinking it (here ~1% differences between table sizes are placement noise, only the ~7% hookup gap repeats across sizes); on the new 227.15 champion the redirect-muxed fetch address already recovers ~355.8K of the 357,527 redirect slots (~4.136M cycles vs this predictor's 4.202M), so the two do not stack and nothing here is worth porting for IPC — this build is only the known-good fallback if imem ever becomes a real combinational or registered memory where r4s1's compare -> fetch-address mux stops being Fmax-free — and this is the third round in a row in which two slots aimed at the same wall or the same bubbles threw away one correct win.

title: Fetch skid buffer: keep the word fetched during back-end stalls (load-use, dmem stall) instead of discarding and re-fetching it
motivation:
Fmax micro-opts are exhausted on this champion: the ~10.7 ns wall is a
three-way tie (ALU loop, regfile-read leg, load-data leg, all ending in the
ID bypass mux) and the last two EX-side edits moved the median by +1.2 /
-2.6 MHz, inside placement noise and far below the 4.6% acceptance bar. The
remaining lever is cycles. Of ~4.136M CoreMark cycles only ~2.9M (estimate
from the stall model, not measured) carry an instruction into ID/EX; the
fetch-limited floor with 22% iStall is N/0.78 ~= 3.72M, so ~0.4M cycles
(~10%) are fetch slots that were READY but thrown away. They are thrown away
in exactly two situations, both of which hold the PC and discard a word that
the bus already delivered:
  (a) load-use bubble (~204K in the ISS trace): the consumer word is in IF,
      is dropped, and is re-fetched next cycle - where it meets a fresh 22%
      chance of an imem stall, so a load-use really costs ~1.28 cycles;
  (b) dmem stall with a LOAD/STORE in MEM (~0.28 cycles per memory op): the
      whole pipeline freezes and the word in IF is dropped the same way.
Because imem and dmem stalls are independent, the pipeline today advances a
memory op only when BOTH buses are ready in the same cycle. Nothing in the
core lets an imem-ready cycle be banked against a later imem stall.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a one-entry skid buffer between imem and decode (in if_stage) so a word
delivered while ID cannot consume it is kept, the PC advances, and fetch
runs one word ahead; a later imem stall is then absorbed by the buffer
instead of becoming a bubble.

State (all flops): buf_valid_q, buf_instr_q[31:0], buf_pc_q[31:0],
buf_ctrl_q (= raw instr[6:4]==3'b110 of the buffered word: BRANCH/JALR/JAL).

Decode source:  in.instr = buf_valid_q ? buf_instr_q : imem_data
                in.pc    = redirect ? redirect_target
                                    : (buf_valid_q ? buf_pc_q : seq_addr)
                opa_pc   = buf_valid_q ? buf_pc_q : seq_addr   (flops only)
io_imemAddr is unchanged (redirect ? redirect_target : seq_addr), still a
function of registers only, as test/cosim/main.cpp requires.

Control (be_stall = dmem_stall | ex_busy | load_use, load_use computed on
the muxed word; ex_ctrl = ID/EX.ctrl.is_branch | is_jump, flops):
  empty, imem_ready, !be_stall : ID consumes the word directly (today's path)
  empty, imem_ready,  be_stall, !ex_ctrl : FILL - buf <= {imem_data, seq_addr},
                                 pc_q <= seq_next, skip_q <= 0
  full,  be_stall              : hold buffer and PC
  full, !be_stall              : ID consumes the buffer; if imem_ready and
                                 !buf_ctrl_q the newly fetched word refills
                                 the buffer and the PC advances, otherwise
                                 buf_valid_q <= 0 and the PC holds
  id_bubble's imem term becomes !(buf_valid_q | imem_ready).

Key invariant that keeps this cheap and safe: buffer full => no branch/jump
in EX => redirect = 0. Fills are refused while ID/EX holds a branch/jump,
and fetch-ahead stops when the word leaving the buffer is a branch/jump
(the pipeline drops back to today's direct mode for the cycle the branch
resolves). So the zero-bubble redirect, skip_q, redirect_kill and the
ZB_PC_LEG_LATE=0 fallback are untouched, no wrong-path word is ever
buffered, there is no flush logic, and a fill can never cost a cycle - it
either pays off (an imem stall arrives while the buffer is full) or is
neutral. RVFI, the bypass network, EX/MEM/WB are not changed.

Sizing (analytic, NOT simulated - the implementer should confirm with
NRET=1 cosim cycle counts before spending P&R time): fill opportunities
~= 204K load-use + ~120K dmem-stall cycles with imem ready and no branch in
EX; ~65% find the buffer empty; each fill pays off with probability
0.22 / (1 - 0.78*(1 - p_ctrl)) ~= 0.6. That is ~125K cycles = ~3% for the
one-entry buffer. This alone is below the acceptance bar, so two cheap
extensions are part of the plan, each to be kept only if cosim shows gain:
  1. second entry behind the first (decode still reads only the head, so no
     extra mux level): fills no longer blocked by a full buffer, ~+1.5%;
  2. conditional BRANCH in the head predicted not-taken (keep fetching
     ahead; a taken branch then uses the existing redirect -> id_bubble
     gate, 1 bubble, target word goes to the buffer). Worth it only if the
     not-taken share of branches passing in full mode exceeds ~40%; JAL/JALR
     always stop fetch-ahead.
Free rider: gate the load-use comparators with raw-opcode use bits
(use_rs2 = instr[5] & !instr[2]; use_rs1 = !instr[2] | (instr[6] & !instr[3]))
so imm/U/J bits that happen to equal the load's rd stop costing bubbles.

Fmax risk, stated plainly: the 2:1 buffer mux puts one LUT level in front
of the regfile read address, and imem word -> regfile -> ID bypass mux ->
rs1_val_q was the second-worst path (9 cells) on the sibling build, within
a few tenths of a ns of the wall. One extra level there could cost about as
much Fmax as the buffer gains in cycles. Gate on the
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median against the
parent's 93.95 MHz, not on worst-path identity. If the median drops by more
than ~2%: move the mux to the data side - read the regfile with both
candidate addresses (imem word and buffer word, two extra LUT-RAM read
ports) and select with the registered buf_valid_q in the same LUT stage as
the existing x0 / write-first select, so the RAM-read leg keeps its depth;
the bypass-select comparators and imm_gen take the muxed word (they are
shorter than the RAM leg). If it still loses, do not ship the buffer; ship
only the load-use use-bit gating.

title: Elastic front end: 1-entry fetch holding register banks words delivered while ID is held, hiding later imem stalls
motivation:
With redirects at 0 bubbles, the champion's IPC (~0.70; ~4.136M cycles) is
set by bus stalls. The front end is rigid: whenever ID cannot consume
(dmem-stall hold, load-use bubble, DIV busy) the word imem delivers in that
cycle is thrown away and re-requested, and the re-request stalls again 22%
of the time; conversely every imem stall is a full pipeline bubble even if
the back end was idle one cycle earlier. Hold cycles are frequent: ~204K
load-use bubbles (r3s2 ISS trace) plus the dmem-stall holds (roughly 0.28
wait cycles per LOAD/STORE, est. ~0.2-0.25M), i.e. ~0.45M of 4.136M cycles
in which a ready fetch slot is wasted. Banking that word makes back-end
holds and imem stalls overlap instead of add. This is the one remaining
large IPC item that needs no predictor and no cache, and it is orthogonal to
the ALU/bypass Fmax wall work.
(Rejected while preparing this: moving the dmem access into EX to kill the
load-use bubble. fpga/core_bench_si.sv reads dmem asynchronously and it only
maps to BSRAM because the EX/MEM.mem_addr flops are absorbed as the BSRAM
address register; an adder in front of io_dmemAddr would turn the 2048x32
array into LUT-RAM. Do not go there.)

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 1-entry holding register (buf_valid_q, buf_instr_q, buf_pc_q) in
if_stage and decouple "word fetched" from "word consumed by ID".

- ID source: word = buf_valid_q ? buf : bus (select is a flop). A word is
  available when buf_valid_q || imem_ready.
- Fetch address stays a function of registers only (cosim looks the word up
  before eval): redirect ? redirect_target : next un-fetched sequential
  address (pc_q/skip_q scheme kept; pc_q now tracks the fetch side).
- ID does not consume (dmem-stall hold, ex_busy, load-use) and the bus is
  ready and the buffer is empty: capture the bus word into the buffer and
  advance the fetch address, instead of dropping it. Buffer full and not
  consumed: fetch address holds.
- ID consumes the buffered word: the bus word of the same cycle (if ready)
  refills the buffer, so the buffer keeps one word of slack until an imem
  stall cycle spends it (that cycle is no longer a bubble: id_bubble's
  imem_stall term becomes !word_available).
- Redirect: flush the buffer; the redirect cycle itself works as today
  (target word taken straight from the bus, 0 bubbles; ZB_PC_LEG_LATE=0
  instr[2] fallback unchanged). A redirect under dmem stall re-asserts as
  today.
- Load-use compare, regfile read addresses, decoder and imm_gen read the
  muxed word; the op_a pc leg reads the muxed pc (both sources are flops).

Expected IPC: each of the ~0.45M hold cycles banks a word with p=0.78; a
banked word is spent on the next imem stall (p=0.22/cycle) unless a taken
redirect (~1 per 10 cycles) flushes it first, so ~65-70% pay off:
~0.2-0.25M cycles saved, +5 to +6% iter/cycle. Measure with
`NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` cycle count before any timing run.

Fmax risk and the plan for it: the muxed word adds one LUT at the head of
the imem-word -> regfile read -> bypass -> rs1_val_q leg, which is tied on
the ~10.7 ns wall (r4s0, r4s2). Gate on the
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median vs the 93.95 MHz
parent. If it drops more than ~2%, remove the level instead of shrinking
the feature: give the buffered word its own regfile read ports addressed
from the buf_instr_q flops (early) with its own bypass-select comparators,
and fold the source select into the existing early mux level
(rs?_pre = (sel_al | buf_valid_q) ? early_val : regs[bus_rs]) so the bus
leg keeps today's depth; decoded ctrl/imm for the buffered word can be
stored decoded (2:1 mux at the non-critical ctrl/imm D pins). Break-even is
~-5% Fmax; if neither form clears +4.6% net, report the cosim cycle count
and the two medians so the IPC number stays usable.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-002-r5s1 (regression, -6.26%): A real regression against the 227.15 champion (not a lost race), and the second independent build of a 1-entry fetch holding register to lose this round — sibling hyp-20261125-001-r5s0's skid buffer scored 215.33 (-5.2%) and its scribe timed out, so both are recorded here: r5s0 measured the split as 4,136,024 -> 4,024,340 CoreMark cycles (+2.8% iter/cycle, about half of the +5-6% this hypothesis priced analytically from "~0.45M wasted ready fetch slots x 0.78 x ~0.65 payoff", the ~0.2-0.25M dmem-hold count being an estimate, not a trace) against 93.95 -> 86.66 MHz (-7.8%; +572 LUT4, +136 FF, +40 LUT-RAM; worst path buffer flop `u_if/i0_q` -> regfile read -> ID bypass mux -> DSP-absorbed MUL operand register in 10 cells), and this slot left no notes or cycle/Fmax split, but fitness = Fmax x 1e7 / cycles, so 212.92 means Fmax <= 88.1 MHz even at zero IPC gain and ~85.7 MHz at r5s0's cycle count, i.e. at least -6.3% Fmax either way — so a `buf_valid_q ? buf_instr_q : imem_data` select on the instruction word is not "one cheap LUT": it sits at the head of the imem word -> regfile read address -> ID bypass -> rs?_val_q / DSP operand leg that r4s0 found tied on the ~10.7 ns routing-dominated wall (the timed netlist's imem word is an LFSR flop, so that leg has no slack to donate), and it costs 2-3x what banking fetched words is worth (+2.8% IPC breaks even at only -2.7% Fmax, far inside the hypothesis's assumed -5%); the shipped core.sv feeds the load-use compare and ID from the muxed `if_id_w.instr` (the simple form), and whether the pre-priced fallback (separate regfile read ports addressed from buf_instr_q flops, source select folded into the existing early bypass mux level, ctrl/imm stored decoded) was ever built or timed is not recorded, so that variant is still untested rather than refuted; rules: do not put any mux between the imem word and the regfile read/decode on this core, confirm an IPC estimate with `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` cycle counts before spending P&R time (stall-overlap arithmetic overshot by ~2x here), write the Fmax/cycle split into the implementation notes so a failed slot stays usable, and stop assigning two slots of one round to the same idea — this is the fourth round in a row where that discarded a slot, and the first where both copies lost to the parent.

title: Prediction-directed run-ahead fetch: bimodal+JAL next-PC predictor feeding a 2-3 entry fetch queue so imem words are banked during hold cycles
motivation:
Zero-bubble redirects (r4s1) left a direction predictor nothing to remove,
so the predictor's remaining value is different: letting FETCH RUN AHEAD of
decode. Today fetch and decode are one combinational stage, so an
instruction only enters ID/EX in a cycle where imem is ready (78%) AND the
pipeline is not held. Every hold cycle (dmem stall with a LOAD/STORE in MEM,
load-use, divide: ~0.37M of the 4.136M CoreMark cycles) throws away the
word imem delivered in that cycle (stall_if holds pc_q and it is fetched
again), and every imem stall (22%) is a bubble because nothing is banked.
Throughput is therefore ~0.78 x 0.91 = 0.71 instr/cycle. A small queue
between fetch and decode turns the product into ~min(): a birth-death
model with f=0.78, c=0.91 gives 0.765 instr/cycle for 2 entries (+7.7%)
and 0.775 for 3 (+9.2%). Running ahead needs the next fetch address before
the branch resolves, i.e. a next-PC predictor - without one every taken
branch (357K) would flush the queue and the idea loses.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple fetch from decode with a registered fetch queue steered by the
lean predictor that r4s2 already showed Fmax-neutral on this wall
(64x2 bimodal PHT on pc[7:2] + always-taken JAL by opcode predecode of the
fetched word, +118 LUT4, 94.5 MHz; remaining mispredicts+JALR ~67K).

Front end (if_stage):
  * pc_f register = next fetch address; io_imemAddr = redirect ?
    redirect_target : pc_f (+skip, as today) - still a function of
    registers only (cosim looks the word up before eval()).
  * Predecode the raw fetched word: JAL -> taken; BRANCH -> PHT counter
    msb; JALR / everything else -> not taken. One pc_f + imm_J/imm_B
    adder gives the predicted target; pc_f <= pred_taken ? target : +4
    whenever the word is accepted (imem ready and queue has room).
    Gate predicted-taken with !imm[1] so pc_f stays word-aligned.
  * Fetch queue: head register (the new IF/ID flop that decode, regfile
    read address and the load-use comparator read INSTEAD of raw
    io_imemData - same logic depth as today, since in the timed netlist
    io_imemData is itself an LFSR flop) plus 1-2 skid entries behind it.
    Each entry: instr, pc, pred_taken, pht_ctr, and the not-fetched
    alternative target alt_target[31:2] (r4s2 trick, so EX needs no
    pc+imm adder / target mux for the verify). Fetch accepts a word
    whenever the queue is not full or its head is being consumed, so
    words keep arriving during dmem-stall / load-use / divide holds.
  * Decode consumes the head when ID/EX is not held; an empty head is the
    bubble (replaces the imem_stall term of id_bubble).

Verify / redirect (ex_stage): redirect = (branch_cond != pred_taken) for
branches (two sync-cleared ID/EX bits red_t / red_nt as in r4s2), JALR
always, JAL never (unless predecode was suppressed). redirect_target =
alt_target or the JALR AGU sum. On redirect: queue flushed (sync clear of
valid bits only), the target is fetched in the same cycle through the
existing address mux and lands in the head register, so a mispredict
costs 1 cycle and a correct prediction 0. Keep pc_f's D input a pure 2:1
select behind the late redirect (r4s1 skip_q trick: the target word
fetched in the redirect cycle is treated as predicted-not-taken and
skip_q marks it delivered), so no adder sits behind the branch compare.

PHT training: 9 dedicated flops loaded at the end of EX (train_we,
train_addr = ID/EX.pc[7:2], train_ctr = saturating +/-1) exactly as in
r4s2 - NOT from EX/MEM fields (that hookup cost 6.5% Fmax in 7 builds).

Expected (cycle-level Monte-Carlo model written for this proposal:
2,922,015 instr, 20% load / 8% store, 203,959 load-use pairs, the real
xorshift accept rate 100/128 on both buses, mispredict = 1 flush; its
model of TODAY's core gives 1.429 cycles/instr vs the real 1.4155, so

motivation:
The ~10.7 ns wall is a tie of three legs that all end at the ID bypass
mux (r4s0): EX result loop, load-data leg, and imem word -> regfile read
-> ID mux -> rs?_val_q, which is the one with the most LUT levels (9
cells, no EX logic). Two of those levels are bookkeeping that can be
deleted instead of optimised: the regfile's write-first compare/mux
(w_en && w_addr == rs?_addr ? w_data) and the rs?_addr == 0 zero mux.
EX-side edits are exhausted (r4s0: +1.2 / -2.6 MHz), so the remaining
micro lever is the regfile-read and load-data legs, cut together.
NEGATIVE FINDING while sizing alternatives (do not retry): the timed
bench reads dmem asynchronously (fpga/core_bench_si.sv,
dmem[dmem_addr[12:2]]) and it is a BSRAM only because Gowin absorbs the
EX/MEM.mem_addr flops as its address register. Driving io_dmemAddr from
the AGU adder directly (dmem access in EX, which would remove the ~204K
load-use bubbles) or putting any mux/store-buffer select between that
register and the pins breaks the absorption (64 Kbit of LUT-RAM or a
synthesis abort). io_dmemAddr must stay a bare register output.

title: Retire-at-MEM datapath: regfile written from MEM, WB bypass leg and MEM/WB data flops removed, load aligner on registered one-hot lanes
motivation:

title: Stall-hiding next-fetch word predictor: PC-tagged LUT-RAM replay table, read one cycle ahead, supplies the instruction when imem stalls
motivation:
Branch-direction prediction has nothing left to win on this champion: r4s1's
redirect-muxed fetch address already makes every taken branch/JAL/JALR cost 0
bubbles (4.136M CoreMark cycles for ~2.922M instructions). What is left is
the bus: io_imemReady is low ~21.9% of cycles (~0.905M stalled fetch cycles),
and every design that needs one ACCEPTED bus fetch per instruction is capped
at 2,922,015 / 0.78125 = 3.740M cycles (+10.6%). Round 5 spent three slots
on fetch buffering under that cap and got +2.8% / +3.7% IPC. The only way
below the cap is to not need the bus for a word the core has already seen,
and CoreMark is a handful of tiny loops executed thousands of times. So the
one predictor-shaped structure with real headroom is a predictor of the NEXT
FETCH: predict (statically, from flops) the address fetch will ask for next
cycle, look that address up in a small PC-tagged table of previously fetched
words, and hold the answer in a register so that a stalled bus cycle still
delivers an instruction. Tagged => never wrong, so no recovery logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add rtl/fetch_pred.sv, a direct-mapped "fetch replay" table, and use it only
as a substitute for the bus word in cycles where io_imemReady = 0.

Table: N = 256 entries (sweep 64/128/256 in cosim first), index pc[9:2],
FULL tag pc[31:10] (exactness is not negotiable), 32-bit word, in LUT-RAM
with async read; valid bits in flops (sync clear on reset and whenever a
FENCE/FENCE.I (opcode 0001111) is decoded, the RISC-V way to resynchronise
instruction and data streams).

Prediction (one cycle ahead, flops only): every cycle read the table at
seq_next (= pc_q + 4/8, already computed in if_stage from flops) and
register {hit, word} into pw_q:
  advance (word consumed, no redirect) : pw_q <= table[seq_next]
  hold with a word in hand (load-use / dmem stall / ex_busy while the bus
    or pw_q delivered)                  : pw_q <= {1, current word}
    (this is r5s0's skid function for free: the retry needs no bus)
  hold without a word                   : pw_q <= table[seq_addr] (re-look up)
  redirect                              : pw_q.hit <= 0
The late `redirect` only clears one flop; no 32-bit data depends on it.

Use: instr = io_imemReady ? io_imemData : pw_q.word  (select is the bus
input, never `redirect`), fetch_ok = io_imemReady | (pw_q.hit & !redirect).
hazard_unit's imem_stall becomes !fetch_ok, so in a redirect cycle with a
stalled bus the (sequential-path) pw word is bubbled at ID/EX exactly like
today's undelivered word - `redirect` already reaches the ID/EX clear through
one gate. io_imemAddr stays redirect ? target : seq_addr (registers only),
pc_q/skip_q logic is unchanged apart from stall using fetch_ok.

Fill: per the r4s2 lesson, through dedicated flops at the producing stage:
fill_we_q <= io_imemReady, fill_addr_q <= io_imemAddr, fill_word_q <=
io_imemData; the table is written the following cycle (tag+word+valid
atomically, so a concurrent read sees the old or the new entry, never a mix).

Verification: formal/wrapper_si.sv ties io_imemReady = 1, so riscv-formal
only ever sees the bus leg of the word mux (it must still pass 53/53, and
liveness is untouched), and it never exercises a replayed word. The gate for
the replay path is therefore cosim with --istall/--dstall (test/cosim/main.cpp
diffs every retirement against the ISS; a stale or mis-tagged word shows up
as an insn/pc mismatch) plus the new cocotb unit test. No log.jsonl entry
has tried instruction-word storage of any kind, so this is untested ground.

Expected IPC (MUST be confirmed with `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` cycle
counts before any P&R): sequential fetches are ~76% of all fetches (the
redirect-cycle fetch and the one after it stay bus-only: 2 x 357K of 2.92M);
at ~90% table hit rate that hides ~0.5M of the 0.905M stalled fetch cycles
-> roughly 3.55-3.65M cycles (+13..16% iter/cycle), below the 3.740M floor of
every bus-bound front end. Gate: file the build only if cosim shows
<= 3.80M cycles.

Expected Fmax: the 2:1 word mux sits at the head of the imem word -> regfile
read -> ID bypass -> rs?_val_q/DSP leg, where r5s0/r5s1 measured -6..8% for
the same kind of mux; that loss is pre-priced (net ~ +6..9%). Judge only on
the `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median vs the parent.
Pre-priced fallbacks if the loss exceeds ~8%: (a) store the entry
pre-decoded in pw_q (ctrl_t + imm decoded in the look-ahead cycle) and mux
at the ID/EX D pins / early bypass level instead of in front of decoder and
imm_gen; (b) give pw_q its own two regfile read ports (addressed from pw_q
flops) and fold the source select into the existing early rs?_pre mux
level; (c) shrink to 64 entries. IPC follow-up only if timing allows: also
look up the redirect target (pc+imm adder from ID/EX flops) so the fetch
after a redirect is covered too.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-003-r6s2 (improvement, +17.16%): New champion at 266.13 (~93.75 MHz x 3,522,669 CoreMark cycles vs 93.95 MHz x 4,136,024; formal 53/53, cosim pass with --istall/--dstall; cycle/Fmax numbers from `.tmp/agent-logs/impl.<id>.log`, the notes field being empty again): the 3.740M "fetch-limited floor" that held all three r5 buffering builds to +2.8..3.7% was only a floor for front ends that need one ACCEPTED bus fetch per instruction, and because CoreMark is a few tiny loops re-executed thousands of times, an exact-tagged 256-entry replay table of already-fetched words (tag + word in LUT-RAM, valid bits in flops, read one cycle ahead into a `pw_q = {hit, word}` register that doubles as the skid register on load-use / dmem / divide holds, `instr = io_imemReady ? io_imemData : pw_word`, `imem_stall = !imem_ready && (!pw_hit || redirect)`, full tag so a hit is never wrong and there is no recovery logic) hides the 21.9% imem backpressure on sequential fetches for +17.4% iter/cycle — better than the hypothesis's own 3.55-3.65M estimate, and unlike r5's two 2x-optimistic stall models it was gated on cosim cycle counts before any P&R (sweep on the address-indexed variant, two / one read port: 256 entries 3,502,943 / 3,522,058, 128 3,578,350 / 3,597,921, 64 3,660,269 / 3,675,759, 32 3,703,618 / not run — each halving down to 64 costs ~2.2% and even 32 entries clear the old floor); what made it Fmax-neutral is the reusable part: the literal build that looked the table up at the computed next address (`pc_q -> +4/+8 adder -> 256-deep LUT-RAM read -> 22-bit tag compare -> pw_q`, plus a second RAM copy for the "hold without a word -> re-look up seq_addr" leg) timed at 80.76 MHz on option 0 with 6971 LUT4 (net ~+1.5%, the look-ahead paths among the worst), whereas keying the table by the fetch STATE one step upstream of that address (index and tag straight from the `{skip_q, pc_q[31:2]}` flops, top index bit XOR skip_q, the entry holding the word at that state's seq_next, fill keyed by a registered `key_q` of the last advance through dedicated fill flops as in r4s2, redirect-cycle words never filled) and dropping the re-look-up port (0.55% cycles, half the RAM) gave 91.50 MHz option 0 / ~93.75 scored at 5044 LUT4 — so key a look-ahead table by the registered state that precedes the address so no adder sits in front of the RAM address or tag compare, let the late `redirect` clear only one hit flop (redirect-free `stall_if`, separate `stall_red` for skip_q) with no 32-bit data behind it, and price a second read port in cycles before paying for it in RAM; two earlier rules need correcting on this evidence: +2307 LUT4 (+84%) hooked to the pipeline only through pc_q/skip_q, pw_q and its own fill flops cost no Fmax, which supports r4s2's "hookup, not area" over r3s2's area reading, and the pre-priced -6..8% for a 2:1 select on the instruction word did not appear in the scored median (-0.2%; option 0 read -2.6% with word mux -> regfile read as its worst leg, so the mux does land on the wall), so r5s1's "no mux between the imem word and the regfile read" is too strong — a flop-selected 2:1 between two flop words (in the timed netlist io_imemReady is a bench_stall_gen flop and io_imemData the LFSR flop) is nearly free and r5s0/r5s1's 6-8% came from something else in those builds (not isolated; this is one `--all-options` evaluation and fallbacks (a)/(b) were never built); limits to carry forward: riscv-formal never sees a replayed word (formal/wrapper_si.sv ties io_imemReady = 1), so any later edit to pc_q/skip_q semantics, the stall terms or the table must be gated on `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` with stalls plus test/test_fetch_pred.py, 53/53 proving nothing about that leg, and core-level cocotb tests list RTL sources explicitly so a new module must be added to test_pipeline.py / test_redirect.py; stale words are excluded only across a decoded FENCE/FENCE.I whose flush lands over two cycles (a store rewriting the instruction right behind the FENCE can still replay stale); area is now half the 10,000 LUT4 target of core.yaml (128 entries is the measured shrink at -2.2% cycles, never timed); and of the ~600K non-retiring cycles left (3,522,669 for 2,922,015 instructions) the split is arithmetic, not a trace — roughly 0.37-0.4M back-end holds (the ~204K load-use bubbles plus dmem stalls and divides) and ~0.16-0.2M fetch stalls the table cannot hide because the redirect-cycle fetch and the one after it stay bus-only (2 x 357K fetches x 21.9%) plus cold/conflict misses — so the unbuilt redirect-target look-up (pc+imm from ID/EX flops) is worth at most ~5% and sits at the 4.6% acceptance bar: cosim-price it first and keep its 32-bit data out from behind the late redirect (r4s1), since fetch is no longer the bottleneck and the larger remaining IPC item is the back-end holds.

title: Load-use bubble trimming: forward the MEM load word into the EX AGU / store data, drop spurious rs2-field matches
motivation:
Fetch is no longer the bottleneck (r6s2). Of the ~600K non-retiring
cycles left (3,522,669 cycles for 2,922,015 instructions) the largest
back-end item that is not a bus wait is the ~204K load-use bubbles
(r3s2 ISS trace). Today EVERY instruction that names a LOAD's rd in
its raw rs1/rs2 field waits a cycle in ID, including consumers that do
not need the value at the start of EX at all:
  (a) LOAD/STORE whose BASE register is the loaded pointer (list
      chasing: lw a5,4(a0); lh a5,2(a5)) - the value is needed only by
      the AGU adder, whose result lands in a flop (EX/MEM.mem_addr);
  (b) STORE whose DATA is the loaded value - needed only at the
      EX/MEM.write_data flop;
  (c) I-type / U-type / J-type words whose imm bits [24:20] happen to
      equal the LOAD's rd (hazard_unit compares the raw rs2 field for
      every opcode) - a pure false positive.
NOTE for whoever reads this: the obvious bigger fix (drive the dmem
bus from the AGU sum in EX so load data is an EX-leg result) was
checked and rejected before filing: fpga/core_bench_si.sv models dmem
as `assign dmem_rdata = dmem[dmem_addr[12:2]]`, which Gowin maps to
BSRAM only by absorbing the EX/MEM.mem_addr flops as the read-address
register. io_dmemAddr must therefore stay a plain flop bank (no adder,
no mux in front of the pins) or the 64 Kbit dmem turns into LUT-RAM.
The same constraint kills store buffers that mux the address pins.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the dmem access in MEM and the address pins on EX/MEM.mem_addr,
but let the three consumer classes above skip the bubble:

1. hazard_unit: load_use = id_ex_mem_read && rd != 0 &&
     ( rs1_match && !exempt_rs1  ||  rs2_match && uses_rs2 && !exempt_rs2 )
   with raw-opcode-bit classes of the fetched word (no decoder output):
     memop_raw  = !i[6] & !i[4] & !i[3] & !i[2]        (LOAD / STORE)
     uses_rs2   = i[5] & !i[2] & !(i[6] & i[4])         (OP/STORE/BRANCH)
     exempt_rs1 = memop_raw & (ID/EX.ctrl.mem_width == 2)   (producer is LW)
     exempt_rs2 = memop_raw & i[5]                      (STORE data, any width)
   rs1 of every opcode stays conservative (LUI/AUIPC/JAL false matches
   are left alone to keep the term small).
2. id_stage: two new sync-cleared ID/EX control bits (same reset /
   bubble / hold block as ctrl_q): fwd_base_q = LOAD-in-EX rd match on
   rs1 & exempt_rs1, fwd_sdata_q = match on rs2 & exempt_rs2. The
   operand registers capture whatever the bypass mux gives (stale,
   never used). The EX-leg selects are unchanged; nothing is added to
   the 32-bit bypass muxes.
3. ex_stage: the instruction in EX with fwd_* set always has its
   producer LOAD in MEM in the same cycle (they entered back to back
   and share every hold).
     agu_addr          = (fwd_base ? dmem_rdata : rs1) + imm   -> EX/MEM.mem_addr
     EX/MEM.write_data = fwd_sdata ? mem load_data (aligned) : rs2
     EX/MEM.rs1_val / rs2_val get the same forwarded values (RVFI only).
   The raw word is used for the base (producer is LW, so no aligner in
   front of the adder). The JALR target and jalr_lo get their OWN
   rs1 + imm adder so the BSRAM-read -> mux -> adder leg ends only at
   the mem_addr register and never reaches redirect_target / pc_q.
   A dmem stall holds EX/MEM (existing stall_ex_mem), so the forwarded
   value is captured exactly in the cycle the bus delivers.
Expected new timed leg: BSRAM tC2Q 2.26 ns -> 2:1 mux -> 32-bit carry
chain -> mem_addr (BSRAM address register), BSRAM to BSRAM, ~8.5 ns
estimated against the ~10.7 ns wall; store-data leg is BSRAM ->
aligner -> 2:1 mux -> flop, shorter than today's load leg into ID.

Sizing is NOT traced: the consumer-class split of the 204K bubbles is
unknown (list code is pointer-chasing, matrix / state code is

  step 0 (before any P&R): implement, run `NRET=1 make cosim

title: Two-path fetch replay: taken-target word pair keyed by the branch's fetch state hides imem stalls across redirects
motivation:
Champion: 3,522,669 CoreMark cycles for 2,922,015 instructions at ~93.75 MHz. The r6s2 replay table
hides the 21.9% imem backpressure only on SEQUENTIAL fetches: `redirect` clears pw_hit, so the fetch
in the redirect cycle and the fetch after it are bus-only. With ~357K redirects that is about
2 x 357K x 0.28 (geometric retry) = ~0.16-0.2M bubbles, a third of the ~600K non-retiring cycles left
and the only large item that needs no back-end change (the back end's wall is the EX-result / load-data
-> ID bypass mux loop, and dmem_addr must stay a bare EX/MEM flop because Gowin absorbs it into the
dmem BSRAM address register, so store buffers / data-side muxes are off the table).
The naive fix (look the table up at pc+imm from ID/EX) puts an adder + RAM read + tag compare behind
the branch and needs a late redirect-selected instruction word; r6s2 measured that shape at 80.8 MHz.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the front end supply the next word for BOTH successor paths from registered state, chosen one
cycle ahead by a predecode, so `redirect` still only gates a 1-bit kill.

1. New taken-path table T2 in fetch_pred.sv (64 entries first; sweep 32/64/128), LUT-RAM + valid flops,
   indexed and fully tagged by the SAME flop-only key the existing table uses, {skip_q, pc_q[31:2]} =
   the fetch state in which a BRANCH/JAL word B is fetched sequentially. Entry = {tag, w0, w1}:
   w0 = word at B's pc-relative target, w1 = word at target+4. Target of BRANCH/JAL is a pure function
   of B's pc and word, so a full-key hit is never wrong (same argument and same FENCE flush as T1).
   JALR never uses T2. No adder in front of any RAM address or tag compare.
2. In the cycle B is in ID (advance), T1 and T2 are read in parallel. A raw-opcode predecode of the
   fetched word picks which one loads pw_q: pred_taken = JAL | (BRANCH & instr[31]) (static BTFN;
   optional untagged 1-bit "forward branch was taken last time" hint read from T2's RAM - prediction
   bits affect only performance, never correctness). pw_q <= pred_taken ? {T2.hit, T2.w0} :
   {T1.hit, T1.word}; new flops pw_tgt_q <= pred_taken, nx_q <= {T2.hit1, T2.w1}.
3. Next cycle (B in EX): the instruction-word mux is UNCHANGED (imem_ready ? imem_data : pw_word).
   Only the validity changes: imem_stall = !imem_ready && !(pw_hit && (pw_tgt_q == redirect));
   stall_if (computed for redirect=0) uses pw_hit && !pw_tgt_q; stall_red uses
   !(imem_ready || (pw_hit && pw_tgt_q)) || dmem_stall. So the late `redirect` reaches id_bubble
   through one XNOR, exactly the depth it has today, and never selects the instruction word.
4. On a consumed redirect, pw_q <= nx_q (word for target+4, the skip_q=1 state), pw_tgt_q <= 0.
   Primary form: `redirect` is a 2:1 select in front of pw_word_q, the same shape as the existing
   pc_q mux (flop -> mux -> flop). A/B alternative if that costs Fmax: keep nx_word_q separate and
   add a flop `use_nx_q` as a registered select on the word mux. A redirect held by a dmem stall keeps
   pw_q/nx_q (idempotent re-assert); a mispredicted direction behaves exactly like today's miss
   (bus-only, one bubble only if the bus is also stalled); redirect_kill words clear the hit.
5. Fill through dedicated flops (r4s2/r6s2 rule): on a redirect by a non-JALR with key_valid_q,
   tkey_q <= key_q (B's key). The first bus word delivered at the target address fills w0+tag+valid,
   the first bus word delivered at target+4 (tracked by advance count; aborted by another redirect or
   flush) fills w1 + valid1. Words are written the cycle after they are produced.

Expected: BTFN + JAL cover roughly 65-75% of redirects (r4s2: static backward-taken got 5.45 of the
8.6 points available), the hint bit up to ~85%; ~0.13-0.17M cycles removed = +4..5% iter/cycle,
Fmax-neutral by the r6s2 precedent (hookup only via pc_q/skip_q, pw_q and private fill flops).

Gates, in this order: (a) extend test/test_fetch_pred.py, then `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` with
--istall --dstall BEFORE any P&R; sweep BTFN vs hint bit and 32/64/128 entries; continue only if
cycles <= ~3.37M (formal ties io_imemReady=1 and proves nothing about replay, so cosim CRCs are the
correctness gate; still run formal/run_all.sh early). (b) `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` median must stay >= ~92.5 MHz; if not, A/B the step-4 variants and drop w1/nx_q
(w0-only is worth about half) before shrinking tables. Record cycle count and Fmax split in
implementation_notes.md.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-002-r7s1 (regression, -1.97%): A real loss to the 266.13 champion that splits (numbers from `.tmp/agent-logs/impl.<id>.log` plus the scored fitness, the notes field being empty again) into +3.55% iter/cycle (3,522,669 -> 3,401,879 CoreMark cycles; formal 53/53, cosim pass with --istall/--dstall) against -5.3% Fmax (93.75 -> ~88.75 MHz scored median, option 0 91.50 -> 86.17, 9 -> 11 logic levels) for +1129 LUT4 / +230 FF / +92 LUT-RAM: the separate taken-path table T2 ({tag, w0} + w1 in LUT-RAM on the same flop-only `{skip_q, pc_q[31:2]}` key, raw-opcode BTFN + JAL predecode loading `pw_q <= pred_taken ? T2 : T1`, plus `pw_tgt_q`, `nx_q` and `pw_q <= nx_q` on a consumed redirect) works as designed, but the redirect-fetch pool is smaller than its arithmetic — 120,790 cycles removed against 0.13-0.17M predicted from a pool priced at 0.16-0.2M (2 x 357K redirect fetches x 0.28), with T2 capacity not the limit (32 / 64 / 128 entries: 3,405,865 / 3,401,879 / 3,400,754) — and sibling hyp-20261125-003-r7s2 attacked the same bubbles with a different mechanism (last-outcome path bit folded into the existing table's key) and by its implementer's report measured +3.17% (3,414,341 cycles; 512 entries reach 3,380,913 = +4.19% but time at 88.14 MHz), so two independent builds price hiding imem stalls across redirects at ~+3.2-3.6% at shippable sizes, under the 4.6% acceptance bar even at zero Fmax cost (this one breaks even at -3.4% Fmax): r6s2's "at most ~5%" was an upper bound, not an estimate, and this pool should not be refiled standalone (the untagged hint bit was never built and r7s2's dynamic variant did no better at 256 entries, so the implementer's "direction prediction is the limit" reading is unconfirmed); the Fmax half shows "Fmax-neutral by the r6s2 precedent" does not transfer once the `pw_word_q` D input stops being one RAM read behind a 1-bit hit clear: a second table read in parallel, a 32-bit T1/T2 select driven by a predecode of the late fetched word (same cone as `advance`) and the late `redirect` as a 2:1 in front of the 32 `pw_word_q` flops (the hypothesis's "same shape as the pc_q mux") put a path the implementer reports as new, `pc_q -> T1/T2 LUT-RAM read -> select -> redirect mux -> pw_word_q` in 9 cells, within 13 ps of the unchanged op_b_q -> ALU -> ID bypass -> rs1_val_q wall on option 0 (16.886 vs 16.899 ns), though which of the three costs the scored median was not isolated (options 1/2 never inspected) because the planned A/Bs (registered `use_nx_q` select instead of the redirect mux, w0-only without `nx_q`/w1, T2 = 32 at ~4K cycles) were never built — the build went to P&R after missing its own "continue only if <= ~3.37M" cosim gate, the r7s0 rule again — and r7s2 keeping ~90% of the same cycles for +85 LUT4 at -1.9% Fmax (91.99 MHz) says that if redirect replay is ever bundled with a larger change, extend the existing table's key rather than add a parallel table and a second 32-bit word register; reusable if a {w0, w1} pair table is built again: a hit must not rewrite w0 (the write clears valid1 and would drop the target+4 word on every re-execution), w1 may only be written by a fill run that owns the slot's tag (wrote w0 itself, or hit at look-up with no w0 write since — otherwise an aliasing run pairs one branch's tag with another's word), and leaving `fence_dec = imem_ready || pw_hit` keeps `redirect` out of the flush term at the price of a performance-only spurious flush on a wrong-path replay word.

title: Path-keyed fetch replay: last-outcome redirect prediction folded into the replay table so redirect-target and target+4 fetches also survive imem stalls
motivation:
The champion's replay table (fetch_pred.sv) hides the 21.9% imem backpressure
only on SEQUENTIAL fetches. Every redirect clears pw_q.hit, so the two fetches
after each of the ~357K taken branches/jumps (the target word in the redirect
cycle and the word at target+4 one cycle later) are still bus-only: 2 x 357K x
0.219/0.781 = ~200K expected lost cycles out of 3,522,669 (r6s2 lesson:
"~0.16-0.2M fetch stalls the table cannot hide ... worth at most ~5%").
The r6s2 lesson's sketch for getting them back (look the target up at pc+imm
from ID/EX flops) puts a 32-bit adder in front of the RAM address and needs a
redirect-selected 32-bit word, both of which earlier rounds measured as Fmax
losers (80.8 MHz adder-before-RAM build; r4s1 82.5 MHz late 32-bit data).
This hypothesis recovers the same slots with NO adder, NO second RAM / read
port and NO 32-bit data behind the late redirect, by predicting the redirect
one cycle ahead with a 1-bit last-outcome predictor that lives inside the
existing table entry.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Generalise the replay table from "word at the next SEQUENTIAL address of fetch
state S" to "the word that actually followed the word fetched in state S last
time, plus one bit saying whether it followed via a redirect".

Data structures (fetch_pred.sv):
  entry  = {tag, tgt, word}      (+1 bit: tgt = this word was delivered in a
                                  redirect cycle, i.e. it is the target word
                                  of the instruction consumed under the key)
  pw_q   = {hit, tgt, word}      (+1 flop pw_tgt_q = prediction "the cycle in
                                  which this word is needed will be a redirect
                                  cycle")
  key    = {pw_tgt_q, skip_q, pc_q[31:2]}  (+1 key bit P = predicted path of
           the CURRENT cycle; all flops; fold P into the index by XOR with
           one more index bit and store it in the tag)
Meaning of entry[{P,S}]: P=0: the consumed word is the one at seq_addr(S);
P=1: the consumed word is the redirect target of the instruction just before
seq_addr(S) (in every redirect cycle the redirector is the instruction that
was consumed last, so S identifies it). The entry holds the NEXT delivered
word and whether that next delivery was itself a redirect delivery.

Use (if_stage / hazard_unit) - the instruction word mux is UNCHANGED
(instr = imem_ready ? imem_data : pw_word, flop select):
  replay usable  = pw_hit && (pw_tgt == redirect)
  imem_stall     = !imem_ready && !(pw_hit && (pw_tgt == redirect))
                   (today: !imem_ready && (!pw_hit || redirect) - same depth,
                    redirect already feeds this term)
  stall_if  (no-redirect path, flops only) = ... || !(imem_ready || (pw_hit && !pw_tgt))
  stall_red (redirect path, flops only)    = !(imem_ready || (pw_hit && pw_tgt)) || dmem_stall
So a correctly predicted taken branch gets its target word from pw_q in the
redirect cycle when the bus stalls (0 bubbles instead of 1.28 expected), and
the look-up done in that same cycle under key {P=1,S} loads pw_q with the
word at target+4 (or the next target if the target word redirects again), so
the following fetch is covered too. From target+8 on the existing
{skip=1,pc=target} keys take over exactly as today.

pw_q update on a consume event (word captured into ID/EX):
  pw_hit_q  <= table_hit && (pw_tgt_q == redirect)   // late redirect -> 1 flop
  pw_tgt_q  <= table_hit && (pw_tgt_q == redirect) && ent.tgt   // 1 flop
  pw_word_q <= ent.word                                // no redirect term
The load-enable / select of pw_word_q uses the PREDICTED path only
(consume_p = pw_tgt_q ? (!stall_red && !redirect_kill) : !stall_if, flops +
bus handshake), because whenever pw_tgt_q != redirect the hit bit is cleared
and the word is don't-care. Late `redirect` therefore reaches only pw_hit_q,
pw_tgt_q, one key_q bit and one fill-flag flop - never 32-bit data (r4s1 rule).
Hold cycles keep the skid behaviour: bus word delivered while holding ->
pw_q <= {1, redirect, imem_data}.

Exactness (no recovery logic, a hit is still never wrong):
  * A tgt=1 entry is filled only when the redirecting instruction in EX is NOT
    a JALR (ID/EX.ctrl.is_jalr flop, exported from ex_stage as one wire):
    branch/JAL targets are a fixed function of the instruction word, JALR
    targets are not. Keys with P=1 are likewise only recorded for non-JALR
    redirects. JALR redirects (13.7K returns etc.) behave exactly as today
    (hit cleared, key_valid cleared).
  * Make the fetch state in every redirect cycle unique to the redirector:
    on redirect && dmem_stall HOLD pc_q/skip_q instead of loading the target
    (the held branch re-asserts the same redirect anyway; imem_addr stays
    redirect ? target : seq_addr, registers only; pc_q D stays a pure 2:1
    select, dmem_stall is a flop-only term in the enable). A redirect that is
    not consumed for any other reason (bus stalled without a usable replay
    word, or the raw instr[2] kill class) keeps today's path: pc_q <= target,
    skip_q <= 0, pw_hit <= 0, pw_tgt <= 0, key_valid <= 0.
  * Fill: key_q <= {redirect, skip_q, pc_q} at each consume event (actual
    path, not predicted), key_valid_q cleared on JALR redirect / unconsumed
    redirect; the next bus-delivered word is written through the existing
    dedicated fill flops with fill_tgt_q <= redirect, suppressed when
    redirect && is_jalr. FENCE flush unchanged.

Prediction quality: tgt is a last-outcome direction bit per fetch state (JAL
always right after first sight). Relative to today a correct "taken"
prediction saves ~0.56 cycles (2 fetches x 0.28), a wrong "taken" prediction
costs ~0.56 (the sequential word and the next look-up are lost), a wrong
"not taken" costs nothing. Upper bound ~190K cycles (+5.4%); with loop-exit /
data-dependent flips priced at ~20-25% of redirects, expect 110-150K cycles
= +3.2..4.4% iter/cycle at unchanged Fmax (only +1 RAM bit column, +~6 flops,
a handful of LUTs; hookup to the pipeline stays pc_q/skip_q/pw_q + one
ID/EX ctrl flop).

Gating and pre-priced options (implementer: do these in order, cosim before
any P&R, as r6s2 did):
  1. `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` with --istall/--dstall: record CoreMark
     cycles. Ship threshold: <= 3.39M cycles (>= +3.9%); the table is exact,
     so CRCs must be unchanged.
  2. If the gain is short because loop exits flip the bit (2 misses per loop
     execution): add 1-bit hysteresis as a 256-flop `weak_q` array beside
     valid_q (a contradicting fill first sets weak and keeps the entry; a
     second one overwrites) - no RAM change. Price it in cosim.
  3. If conflict misses grow (P=1 keys and the {skip=1} aliases add rows to
     256 entries): try IDX_W=9 in cosim; r6s2 measured ~2.2% per halving, and
     +2.3K LUT4 of table cost no Fmax there. Time with
     `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` only after cosim
     says it is worth it.
  4. Fmax gate is the --all-options median vs the parent (93.75 MHz), not the
     identity of the worst path. If it drops: first A/B the redirect&&dmem_stall
     pc_q hold (alternative: keep today's pc_q load and instead clear
     key_valid/pw_hit on a dmem-held redirect), then the pw_tgt_q index XOR
     (alternative: P only in the tag).
riscv-formal ties io_imemReady=1 and never sees a replayed word, so the
correctness gate for this change is cosim with stalls plus an extended
test/test_fetch_pred.py; still run the full formal suite because pc_q/skip_q
update and the hazard terms are touched.

changes.description: Add tgt bit to entry and pw_q (pw_tgt_q), add predicted-path bit P=pw_tgt_q to the look-up key (tag + index XOR) and actual-path bit to key_q/fill key; pw_hit_q/pw_tgt_q next-state gated by (pw_tgt_q == redirect); pw_word_q load select from predicted path only; fill_tgt_q <= redirect, tgt/P=1 fills and keys suppressed for JALR redirects; new inputs: is_jalr (ID/EX flop), consume/redirect-consumed controls; new output pw_tgt.

Hold pc_q/skip_q on redirect && dmem_stall (state in a redirect cycle is unique to the redirector); pass pw_tgt out and is_jalr / consume controls into fetch_pred; word mux unchanged (imem_ready ? imem_data : pw_word).

title: One 33x33 signed multiplier: a single DSP site for the absorbed rs1/rs2 operand registers
motivation:
Every near-tied leg of the ~10.7 ns, ~73%-routing wall (imem word ->
regfile read -> ID bypass mux; op_b -> ALU -> ID bypass mux; dmem BSRAM ->
aligner -> ID bypass mux) ends at ID/EX.rs1_val_q / rs2_val_q, and Gowin
absorbs those registers into the DSP input registers. alu.sv still builds
THREE 32x32 products (mul_ss / mul_uu / mul_su, 6 DSP), so the late ID
bypass-mux output must route to three fixed DSP-column sites plus the
fabric copies. r4s0 measured the single-multiplier form on an older parent:
correct first try (formal 53/53, cosim pass), DSP 6 -> 2, -131 LUT4,
+1.3% Fmax; inside r6s1's netlist the same edit was worth +6.5 MHz. It was
never ported to the current champion (LESSONS r4s0: "remains a cheap
IPC-neutral port").
Rejected while preparing this (do not retry): issuing the dmem access from
EX straight off the AGU adder to delete the ~204K load-use bubbles. In
fpga/core_bench_si.sv dmem is `assign dmem_rdata = dmem[dmem_addr[12:2]]`
(async read, 2048x32); it is a BSRAM only because Gowin absorbs the
EX/MEM.mem_addr register as the BSRAM read-address register. A
combinational (adder-driven) io_dmemAddr removes that register, so the
memory becomes ~4K LUT-RAM cells on a AGU -> RAM -> aligner -> ID path.
Load data therefore cannot arrive earlier than MEM in the timed netlist,
and io_dmemAddr must stay a plain register output.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the three 32x32 products with ONE 33x33 signed multiply whose
operands come only from flops:
  ma33 = {rs1_sx_q, rs1_val_q},  mb33 = {rs2_sx_q, rs2_val_q}
  prod = $signed(ma33) * $signed(mb33)          (66 bits)
  MUL = prod[31:0];  MULH / MULHSU / MULHU = prod[63:32]
The 33rd bits are registered in id_stage in the SAME reset/CE always_ff
block as rs1_val_q / rs2_val_q (so Gowin can still absorb the whole 33-bit
operand into the DSP input register; a combinational 33rd bit would
un-absorb the port):
  rs1_sx_q <= rs1_val_d[31] & !(instr[13] & instr[12])   // unsigned only for MULHU
  rs2_sx_q <= rs2_val_d[31] & !instr[13]                 // signed for MUL / MULH
(raw funct3 bits; the value is don't-care for non-MUL ops). The
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arms keep reading ma / mb (32-bit) unchanged.
